SUMMARY
This summary aims to give you an overview of the information contained in this prospectus and
should be read in conjunction with the full text of this prospectus. As it is a summary, it does not
contain all the information that may be important to you. You should read the whole prospectus,
including our financial statements and the accompanying notes, before you decide to invest in the
Offer Shares. There are risks associated with any investment. Some of the particular risks in
investing in the Offer Shares are set out in ‘‘Risk Factors’’ in this prospectus. You should read that
section carefully before you decide to invest in the Offer Shares.
OVERVIEW
Who We Are
We are a leading integrated provider of precision manufacturing solutions, bringing together tools,
materials and intelligent equipment for key process segments of the global printed circuit board (PCB)
fabrication value chain, including drilling, routing/forming and other related precision manufacturing
processes. According to Frost & Sullivan, we are the world’s largest supplier of drill bits as measured by
sales volume. During the Track Record Period, we ranked first globally in terms of sales volume of drill
bits in each of 2023, 2024 and 2025, with global market shares of 26.5%, 26.8% and 29.2%,
respectively. In terms of sales revenue of drill bits, we ranked first globally in 2023, second globally in
2024 and first globally in 2025, with global market shares of 21.4%, 20.8% and 22.9%, respectively. We
strive to create greater value for our customers through high-end intelligent precision manufacturing
solutions, thereby catalyzing progress across global industries.
Our product portfolio spans four major categories consisting of (i) precision cutting tools, (ii)
grinding and polishing materials, (iii) functional film materials, and (iv) intelligent computer numerical
control (CNC) equipment. These products serve a broad range of end markets of strategic importance,
including AI infrastructure, embodied robotics, semiconductors and integrated circuit (IC)-related
applications, low-earth-orbit satellite communications, high-end equipment manufacturing and smart
vehicles, as well as certain other industries such as consumer electronics, telecommunications and
industrial control.
Widely regarded as the foundation of the electronics industry, PCBs play a pivotal role in their
manufacturing process. The performance of PCB tools highly depends on the PCB technology
advancement and directly impacts the functionality and reliability of downstream electronic products.
The quality and durability of PCB tools also impact production cost and delivery time, and these effects
cascade through the supply chain to shape the competitiveness and responsiveness of downstream PCB
applications. As a global leading player in selected PCB manufacturing-related tools, materials and
intelligent equipment, we support rapid development of our downstream industries through our
integrated portfolio of tools, materials and intelligent equipment. By providing high-end, reliable and
scalable manufacturing support, we contribute to the high-quality development of the global PCB
industry and the advancement of precision manufacturing and intelligent industrial technologies.

Our Manufacturing and R&D
We have established manufacturing centers in Dongguan, Guangdong Province and Nanyang,
Henan Province, covering selected product lines of integrated tools, materials and intelligent equipment
and reinforcing our position as the global leader in drill-bit production capacity. Our Thailand
manufacturing base has commenced mass production. In 2025, we acquired the business of MPK
Kemmer to accelerate our expansion into Germany and the broader European market. We also plan to
increase investment in Asia and Europe to build a global operating network spanning R&D, production,
sales and service.
Our R&D is closely integrated with production. Leveraging production experience, market insights
and our independently developed production equipment, we use data simulation, modelling and
experimental validation to advance key processes and materials, address technical bottlenecks and
enhance product competitiveness. As of December 31, 2025, we had 491 R&D personnel, including
senior specialists in precision tool manufacturing, materials, coating and equipment engineering, some of
whom hold advanced qualifications and have led national and provincial key research projects.
Our Market Opportunities
Our market opportunities are underpinned by steady growth in global PCB demand and a structural
shift toward high-end applications. According to Frost & Sullivan, the global PCB market as measured
by revenue is expected to increase from US$93.2 billion in 2026 to US$114.8 billion in 2030,
representing a CAGR of 5.3%, driven by AI, data centers, next-generation communications, autonomous
driving and AR/VR. Within this broad market, higher-value product segments such as high-layer count
boards, HDI boards and IC substrates are expected to outpace the market’s average growth, with forecast
CAGRs of 7.4%, 6.7% and 6.9%, respectively, from 2026 to 2030, driven by increasing demand for
high-density interconnect (HDI) and high-performance signal integrity.
The rapid build-out of AI infrastructure is creating large-scale demand for high-performance PCBs
manufactured by our customers, which in turn drives demand for our PCB tools and related products. In
2025, the server segment accounted for approximately US$15.8 billion of global PCB revenue, and this
segment is expected to remain amongst the fastest growing over the next five years as AI servers, large-
scale data centers and high-performance computing continue to scale, according to Frost & Sullivan.
These applications require PCBs with higher layer counts, finer lines and spaces, smaller via diameters
and tighter positional tolerances. As a result, these trends directly drive up both the consumption volume
and the performance requirements of PCB drilling and cutting tools, especially microdrills, high length-
to-diameter ratio drilling tools and advanced coated drills, where we have established leading positions.
As a global leader in selected PCB manufacturing-related tools, materials and intelligent
equipment, with an extensive self-developed equipment base and expanding international footprint, we
believe we are positioned to capture these market opportunities.
Our Financial Highlights
We have achieved steady growth during the Track Record Period. Our revenue increased by 19.9%
from RMB1,295.1 million in 2023 to RMB1,552.6 million in 2024. Our revenue further increased by
34.2% to RMB2,084.2 million in 2025, primarily due to the increase in revenue generated from
precision cutting tools.

We believe that the following strengths contribute to our success: (i) Comprehensive portfolio
across tools, materials and intelligent equipment, supported by large scale manufacturing capabilities;
(ii) Strategically positioned to capture AI-driven PCB growth through stable and close relationships with

We are implementing the following strategies: (i) Deepen our portfolio of ‘‘tools, materials and

manufacturing capacity to enhance supply chain resilience and increase market share in premium
overseas markets; (iv) Advance industry-chain integration and pursue selective mergers and acquisitions
to accelerate expansion; and (v) Build a talent strategy commensurate with rapid growth and
globalization.

RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
We are committed to technological innovation to enhance our capabilities and deliver value to
customers, while supporting growth in our sales and profitability. We maintain a dedicated R&D team
that integrates profound theoretical knowledge, technical expertise, and practical experience. As of
December 31, 2025, our R&D team consisted of 491 employees. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our R&D
expenses were RMB97.7 million, RMB109.6 million and RMB135.9 million, respectively, representing
approximately 7.5%, 7.1% and 6.5% of our total revenue for the respective years.
OUR PRODUCTION
We primarily adopt an in-house manufacturing model, supplemented by a minor portion of
subcontracted processing for certain non-core processes. Standard products, including drill bits and
milling cutters, are generally produced under a market-driven make-to-stock model based on production
schedules prepared by our Supply Management & Planning Department and adjusted for demand and
inventory levels. Products such as grinding and polishing materials and intelligent CNC equipment are
generally produced on a make-to-order basis after customer order confirmation. Throughout the process,
our Quality Department implements controls over raw materials, semi-finished products and finished
products to ensure product consistency, stability and timely delivery.
SALES AND MARKETING
During the Track Record Period, we sold our products through three primary channels: (i) direct
sales, (ii) sales through channel partners and (iii) sales through agents. We generally enter into sales and
purchase agreements pursuant to customer purchase orders. We have also entered into framework supply

COMPETITION
According to Frost & Sullivan, the global PCB drilling tools industry is highly competitive and
relatively concentrated, with the top five drill bit manufacturers in the industry accounting for
approximately 75.7% of the total market share in terms of sales volume in 2025. We ranked first among
the PCB drill bit manufacturers in terms of sales volume in 2024 and 2025 with global market shares of
26.8% and 29.2%, respectively. We believe that our competitive position is underpinned by our
strengths, including our market position, exceptional R&D capabilities, key technologies and
experienced management team. See ‘‘Industry Overview.’’

Non-IFRS Financial Measure
To supplement our consolidated financial statements, which are presented in accordance with
IFRS, we also use adjusted net profit (non-IFRS measure) as additional financial measures, which is not
required by, or presented in accordance with IFRS. We believe the non-IFRS measure facilitates
comparisons of operating performance from year to year and company to company by eliminating
– 7 –

=== PAGE 18 ===
SUMMARY
potential impacts of certain items. We believe this measure provides useful information to investors and
others in understanding and evaluating our consolidated results of operations in the same manner as they
help our management. However, such non-IFRS financial measure we presented may not be directly
comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. The use of this non-IFRS measure should
not be considered as a substitute for analysis of our results of operations or financial condition as
reported under IFRS.
We define adjusted net profit for the years (non-IFRS measure) as net profit for the years adjusted
by adding back share-based payment expenses. The following table reconciles our adjusted net profit for

RISK FACTORS
Our business and offering involve certain risks as set out in ‘‘Risk Factors.’’ You should read that
section in its entirety carefully before you decide to invest in our H Shares. Some of the major risks we
face include: (i) Our results are dependent on demand from downstream electronics end-markets.
Weakness or disruption in any of these sectors could materially and adversely affect us; (ii) Our growth
and profitability depend on general economic conditions, which in turn may influence the development
of the industries our customers serve; (iii) The industries in which we operate are highly competitive. If
we fail to compete effectively and successfully, our business, results of operations and financial
condition may be materially and adversely affected; (iv) We may not be able to derive the desired
benefits from our research and development efforts, which may impact our profitability and may not
generate the results we expect to achieve; and (v) Our international operations expose us to additional
risks that could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. Our business
may remain subject to risks relating to international trade restrictions, export controls, tariff policies and
sanctions imposed by the United States and other foreign jurisdictions from time to time, which may
affect our operations and market environment. For further details, see ‘‘Risk Factors — We may be
subject to risks associated with international trade restrictions, including sanctions and export controls,
and our reputation, business, results of operations and financial condition could be adversely affected.’’
OUR LISTING ON THE CHINEXT OF THE SHENZHEN STOCK EXCHANGE
Our Company has been listed on the ChiNext of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange since November
2022. Since that listing and up to the Latest Practicable Date, there had been no instance of material
non-compliance with the rules of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange or other applicable PRC securities laws
and regulations in any material respect. Our PRC Legal Advisor is of the view that the Directors’
confirmation in this regard is accurate and reasonable, and nothing has come to the attention of the Joint
Sponsors that would cause them to disagree with that confirmation.

DIVIDENDS AND DIVIDEND POLICY
As of December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, we declared dividends of RMB90.2 million, RMB82.0
million and RMB278.8 million respectively. On April 16, 2026, we approved a final dividend in respect
of the year ended December 31, 2025 of RMB205.0 million, including tax. The dividend was not
recognized as a liability as of December 31, 2025. Such final dividend had been paid in full by June 4,
2026. No other dividend was paid or declared by our Company or other entities comprising our Group
during the Track Record Period. Our dividend policy provides that, in principle, the specific dividend
ratio shall be determined by our Board in accordance with applicable laws and regulations and our
operating conditions, and approved at a general meeting of our Shareholders. We do not have a fixed
dividend payout ratio. Subject to compliance with applicable PRC laws and our Articles of Association,
dividends may be distributed in the form of cash dividends, stock dividends or a combination of both,
with priority given to cash dividends where conditions permit. Any proposed dividend distribution will
take into account our results of operations, financial condition, capital requirements, significant
investment plans and the interests of our Shareholders.

RECENT DEVELOPMENT AND NO MATERIAL ADVERSE CHANGE
Recent Development
Subsequent to the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we maintained stable
business operations and development. Based on our unaudited management accounts for the three
months ended March 31, 2026, our revenue amounted to RMB756.1 million, and our gross profit
amounted to RMB375.7 million, representing a gross profit margin of approximately 49.7%. During the
same period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, our production and sales operations remained stable,
and we did not experience any material adverse change in our major product sales, production capacity,
production utilization, procurement by major customers or order fulfilment.
As part of our continued efforts to expand our domestic manufacturing footprint, we have
developed a new production facility at our Liaoxia Area II production base in Dongguan, Guangdong
Province. The new facility has a gross floor area of approximately 73,500 sq.m. and is primarily used
for the production of drill bits, with a designed production capacity of approximately 960.0 million drill
bits per year. As of the Latest Practicable Date, the new facility had completed the relevant inspection
and acceptance procedures and commenced phased operations. We expect to ramp up production
capacity progressively on a rolling basis.
On June 5, 2026, following the expiry of the applicable lock-up arrangements in respect of the
relevant A Shares held by Zhejiang Taiding, one of the Controlling Shareholders, disposed 10,285,323
A Shares, representing approximately 2.50% of the total issued share capital of the Company as of June
5, 2026, to eligible investors in the A-share market through a market-based inquiry process (the ‘‘A
Share Selldown’’). The A Share Selldown was conducted solely at the shareholder level, did not involve
any issuance of new Shares by our Company and, accordingly, we did not receive any proceeds from it.
The A Share Selldown was not undertaken for the purpose of, or in connection with, the Global
Offering. The final sale price under the A Share Selldown is not linked to, and does not determine, set
any cap or floor for, or otherwise constrain, the Offer Price range. Other than Zhejiang Taiding as the
selling Shareholder, no other entity comprising our Controlling Shareholders, sold any Shares in, or
otherwise participated as a selling Shareholder in, the A Share Selldown. Accordingly, the A Share
Selldown did not result in any change in control of the Company or any material adverse impact on the
Company’s corporate governance, business operations or prospects.
No Material Adverse Change
Our Directors confirm that, up to the date of this Prospectus, there has been no material adverse
change in our business, financial condition and results of operations since December 31, 2025, which is
the end date of the years reported on in the Accountants’ Report as set out in Appendix I to this
Prospectus, and there is no event since December 31, 2025 which would materially affect the
information in the Accountants’ Report as set out in Appendix I to this Prospectus.

GLOSSARY
This glossary of technical terms contains explanations of certain technical terms used in this
document in connection with our Company and our business. Such terminology and meanings may
not correspond to standard industry meanings or usages of those terms.
‘‘3C’’ an abbreviation for computers, communications and consumer
electronics; in this prospectus, generally referring to consumer
electronic products such as mobile phones, tablets and related
devices that use PCBs and precision-machined components.
‘‘AGV’’ automated guided vehicle, being an autonomous material-handling
vehicle used in our automated storage and retrieval system for
line-side storage, inbound and outbound operations and inventory
counting in our warehouses and production facilities.
‘‘AI’’ artificial intelligence, being technologies that enable machines
and systems to perform tasks typically requiring human
intelligence, such as perception, pattern recognition, prediction or
decision-making.
‘‘AI infrastructure’’ the combination of data centers, AI servers, high-speed
networking and storage systems, and related hardware and
software that support the training and inference of AI models and
AI-enabled applications.
‘‘AI server’’ a server configured with processors, accelerators and memory
subsystems optimized for AI workloads, including the training
and inference of machine-learning models used in, among others,
data centers and cloud platforms.
‘‘back-drilling’’ a process in which part of a plated through-hole is drilled out
from the opposite side of the PCB.
‘‘cemented carbide’’ a hard, wear-resistant composite material typically made of
tungsten-carbide particles bonded with a metallic binder (such as
cobalt), widely used in the manufacture of drill bits, milling
cutters and CNC tools.
‘‘ceramic brushes’’, types of grinding and polishing brushes used in PCB
‘‘non-woven brushes’’ and manufacturing, differentiated by their brush media (ceramic, non-
‘‘nylon brushes’’ woven fiber or nylon) and used to remove drilling burrs and resin
smear, planarize copper surfaces and clean microvias.
‘‘CNC’’ computer numerical control, being the computerized control of
machine tools in which pre-programmed sequences of machine-
control commands are executed to perform automated machining
operations.
‘‘CNC tools’’ cutting and forming tools mounted on CNC machine tools
(including, among others, diamond tools, milling cutters, reamers,
taps and indexable inserts) that perform milling, turning, drilling
and related operations on metals and composite materials.
– 23 –

=== PAGE 34 ===
GLOSSARY
‘‘coated technology’’ drill bits, milling cutters and other tools whose working surfaces
are coated with thin films such as CVD diamond, PVD wear-
resistant coatings or ta-C coatings to improve wear resistance,
reduce friction and enhance tool life and drilling performance.
‘‘CVD diamond coating’’ a thin diamond layer formed on the surface of a tool by chemical
vapour deposition, used to substantially improve wear resistance
when machining hard or abrasive materials such as ceramic and
aluminium-based substrates.
‘‘drill bit’’ a slender, rotary cutting tool used to drill holes. In PCB
manufacturing, drill bits are used to create microvias and other
holes that form electrical interconnections between PCB layers.
‘‘EHS’’ environmental, health and safe.
‘‘embodied robotics’’ AI-enabled robots that are physically instantiated in hardware
(such as industrial or service robots) and interact with the
physical environment, requiring integrated mechanical, actuation,
control and sensing systems; our products support, among others,
actuation components and precision-machined parts used in such
robots.
‘‘FCBGA’’ flip-chip ball grid array, a type of advanced semiconductor
packaging in which a chip is flipped and connected to a substrate
through solder bumps, with solder balls arranged in a grid array
on the underside of the substrate; used in high-performance
computing, networking and AI infrastructure.
‘‘FC-CSP’’ flip-chip chip-scale package, a compact semiconductor packaging
format in which the die is directly attached to a substrate using
flip-chip interconnects, with an overall size not substantially
larger than the die itself; used in high-density, high-performance
applications where substrate flatness and surface quality are
critical.
‘‘functional film materials’’ films, typically applied to glass or polymer substrates, that
provide optical, protective or functional properties, such as light
control, anti-glare, anti-reflection, privacy protection or scratch
resistance, for applications including backlight modules, lower
polarizers, cover glass, in-vehicle displays, smartphones and PCs.
‘‘grinding and polishing materials’’ consumable abrasive products (such as brush wheels and other
grinding and polishing media) used in PCB manufacturing to
remove burrs and resin smear, planarize copper surfaces, clean
microvias and prepare PCBs for subsequent electroplating,
plugging and circuit-formation processes.
‘‘HDI’’ high-density interconnect, a type of PCB characterized by fine
lines, small vias, high connection pad density and thin dielectrics,
often used in advanced electronics such as smartphones, AI
servers and high-end computing equipment.
– 24 –

=== PAGE 35 ===
GLOSSARY
‘‘high aspect-ratio hole’’ a hole whose depth-to-diameter ratio is relatively large, making
drilling and subsequent metallization more difficult; such holes
are common in high-layer-count PCBs, IC substrates and high-
performance computing boards.
‘‘high-layer-count board(s)’’ multilayer PCB(s) with eight or more conductive layers,
commonly used in high-performance applications such as servers,
network switches and 5G base stations due to their requirements
for high-speed signal transmission, high integration and
reliability.
‘‘HPC’’ high-performance computing, the use of large-scale computing
resources (including AI servers and networking equipment) to
process complex tasks and large volumes of data at high speed.
‘‘IC’’ integrated circuit, an electronic circuit formed on a small
semiconductor chip, containing multiple electronic components
such as transistors and resistors, used in a wide range of
electronic devices and systems.
‘‘IC substrate’’ a high-density interconnect substrate used to mount and
interconnect integrated circuits in packaging (such as FCBGA);
IC substrates provide fine wiring, thermal management and
mechanical support between the semiconductor die and the PCB.
‘‘intelligent CNC equipment’’ our high-precision CNC tool grinders and step cylindrical
grinding machines and other equipment that incorporate multi-
axis CNC control, automation, sensing and closed-loop process
optimization to support the manufacture and regrinding of drill
bits, milling cutters and other precision tools.
‘‘LEO satellite communications’’ communications services provided via satellites operating in low-
earth orbit, typically at altitudes of a few hundred to around
2,000 kilometers, used for broadband connectivity and other
applications and driving demand for high-performance PCBs and
related tools.
‘‘MCPCB’’ metal-core printed circuit board, a PCB in which a metal
(typically aluminum or copper) core is used to improve heat
dissipation, commonly applied in high-power or thermally
demanding applications such as LED lighting and power
electronics.
‘‘microvia’’ a small-diameter hole in a PCB, typically formed by mechanical
or laser drilling, that connects one layer of a PCB to adjacent
layers and is central to HDI PCB structures.
‘‘PCB’’ printed circuit board, a laminated board made of insulating
material and copper layers, used to mechanically support and
electrically connect electronic components using conductive
tracks, pads and other features.
– 25 –

=== PAGE 36 ===
GLOSSARY
‘‘PCB tools’’ specialized cutting and routing tools used in PCB fabrication,
including drill bits, routers, bevel (gold-finger) cutters, chamfer
cutters, countersinks, engraving/V-bits, key-slot/T-slot cutters and
other form tools.
‘‘PVD coating’’ a coating formed by physical vapour deposition, in which a thin
film of wear-resistant material is deposited on the surface of tools
in a vacuum environment, used to reduce tool wear, improve
drilling performance and extend tool life.
‘‘ta-C’’ tetrahedral amorphous carbon, a type of carbon-based coating
with high hardness and low friction, used on drill bits and other
tools to reduce wear and mitigate issues such as inner copper
debris and chip clogging in high length-to-diameter ratio holes.
‘‘V-scoring/V-cut’’ a V-shaped pre-cut or groove made on a PCB panel so that
individual boards can be separated after fabrication.
‘‘VMI’’ vendor-managed inventory, a supply-chain arrangement under
which a supplier manages inventory levels at or near the
customer’s site (often using VMI warehouses) and recognizes
revenue when the customer draws down inventory based on
agreed reconciliation cycles.

lose all or part of your investment. These factors are contingencies that may or may not occur, and

after the date hereof, and is subject to the cautionary statements in the section titled ‘‘Forward-

RISKS RELATING TO OUR BUSINESS AND INDUSTRY
Our results are dependent on demand from downstream electronics end-markets. Weakness or
disruption in any of these sectors could materially and adversely affect us.
We primarily supply precision cutting tools, auxiliary materials and certain equipment used in PCB
manufacturing. Demand for our products therefore depends largely on the performance of downstream
electronics end-markets, including AI servers and data centers, communications and networking, smart
vehicles, semiconductors, high-speed networking, advanced equipment manufacturing and intelligent
robotics. If any of these sectors weakens or is disrupted, our customers may reduce production or defer
capital and consumables spending, which could reduce our sales volumes and pricing and adversely
affect our revenue, financial condition and results of operations.
The electronics end-markets we ultimately serve are cyclical and subject to seasonality and
product-cycle changes. Historically, PCB demand linked to computers and consumer electronics tends to
be stronger in the second half of the year; a weaker season or a down-cycle could reduce our customers’
run-rates and their consumption of PCB drill bits and related consumables. The growth in sectors such
as server and data storage, automotive electronics, mobile phones, computers and consumer electronics
significantly influence the demand for PCBs and our related products. For instance, the rise of AI and
the increasing integration of electronic components in AI servers, high-speed switches and terminal AI
hardware have driven the demand for more sophisticated and high-performance PCBs. There can be no
assurance that periods of end-market strength will persist, and if any of the end-markets we ultimately
serve experiences reduced demand, our business, results of operations and financial condition may be
adversely affected.
In addition, while our customer base is broad, our sales to top customers can be meaningful in any
period. In 2025, our top five customers accounted for approximately 30.8% of our sales. A downturn in
one or more end-markets served by these customers, or changes in their procurement plans, could reduce
our order volumes, increase price pressure, lengthen receivable cycles and result in inventory build-ups.
There can be no assurance that demand from our major customers or the end-markets they operate in
will not decline, and if they do, our business and profitability may be adversely affected.
Our growth and profitability depend on general economic conditions, which in turn may influence
the development of the industries our customers serve.
Our results of operations are affected by overall macroeconomic and financial market conditions,
which in turn influence investment and spending decisions by our customers and the industries they
serve. While demand for our products ultimately relates to electronics end-markets, our growth and
profitability are more directly linked to PCB manufacturers’ capital-expenditure plans, utilization levels
and process-upgrade cycles, all of which are sensitive to general economic conditions. Our products,
such as PCB drill bits, milling cutters and functional films, are used across a wide range of downstream
– 28 –

=== PAGE 39 ===
RISK FACTORS
applications, and our customers’ ability and willingness to expand capacity, upgrade production lines
and adopt our products are influenced by factors such as economic growth, funding availability,
regulatory developments and sector-specific confidence.
As part of our revenue relates to smart devices and automotive, consumer spending materially
affects demand. These investments and spending are in turn affected by factors beyond our control, such
as interest rates, credit availability, unemployment levels, inflation, exchange-rate volatility, trade and
tariff policies, and overall business confidence. Periods of economic uncertainty may delay or reduce
investments in AI server build-outs, automotive platforms or consumer devices, which could reduce
orders for PCBs, in turn, demand for our precision cutting tools and other consumables, thereby
adversely affecting our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Many of our customers face intense competition and continuous pressure to lower their cost per
board and improve throughput and yield. They may frequently raise new technical and cost-down
requirements. In addition, the specialized PCB tools and related consumables markets in which we
operate have relatively low regulatory entry barriers, and as more competitors enter or expand capacity,
market competition may further intensify. If we are unable to meet such expectations through product
performance, delivery and pricing, our prospects, business, results of operations and financial condition
could be adversely affected.
The industries in which we operate are highly competitive. If we fail to compete effectively and
successfully, our business, results of operations and financial condition may be materially and
adversely affected.
The specialized markets in which we operate, including precision cutting tools, grinding and
polishing materials, functional film materials and intelligent CNC equipment, are highly competitive
with numerous domestic and international manufacturers of varying engineering capabilities and product
sophistication, some of which have secured substantial market shares with key customers. According to
Frost & Sullivan, in terms of global PCB drill bit sales volume for 2025, the combined market share of
the top five companies in the global PCB drill bit market was 75.7%. General competition in our
industry is characterized by price competition and rapid technological changes.
We primarily compete with peers on innovation and iteration of technology, products and
production processes, production capacity, supply chain pricing and customer relationships, and failure
to compete successfully on such aspects may adversely affect our results of operations and financial
performance. In particular, we rely on our ability to maintain robust cooperative relationships with
customers and respond rapidly to customer requirements to maintain mutually beneficial relationships
with our existing and new customers. As we expand our product portfolio, customer base and
geographical markets, we will need significant managerial, financial and human resources to exceed our
competitors in these aspects. We cannot assure you that we can maintain our overall competitiveness to
secure sales orders or gain market share.
As our customers seek to improve their manufacturing processes and reduce costs, they may
frequently raise new technical and cost-reduction requirements, such as higher tool life at smaller
diameters, tighter drilling tolerances, faster delivery under consignment models, or better film
performance. If we are unable to meet such expectations through product performance, delivery and
pricing, our prospects, business, results of operations and financial condition could be adversely
affected.
Some of our competitors may have longer operating histories, greater name recognition, larger
customer bases and greater financial, sales and marketing, production, distribution, technical and other
resources and experience than we do. Our competitors’ greater size in some cases may provide them
with a competitive advantage with respect to production costs due to economies of scale and their ability
to purchase raw materials and utilities at lower prices. In addition, our competitors may be able to
devote greater resources to the research and development of technologies, processes and products that
are more effective than ours. Greater resources may allow such competitors to respond to changes in

downturns in the markets where we operate. Intense competition may also lead to further consolidation
in the industry. Our competitors may enter into strategic alliances such as business partnerships or joint

more effectively compete against us. There can be no assurance that we will be able to continue to

We may not be able to derive the desired benefits from our research and development efforts,

To maintain our competitive position and grow our business, we must continually develop, rapidly
update and introduce innovative products for existing and potential customers, including through joint
development projects aligned to customers’ technical roadmaps. The PCB industry is characterized by
ongoing technological change and increasingly complex, diversified requirements. As a result, we place
significant emphasis on R&D, which requires considerable investment in both human resources and
capital. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our R&D expenses were RMB97.7 million, RMB109.6 million and
RMB135.9 million, representing 7.5%, 7.1% and 6.5% of our revenue for the respective years. However,
we cannot assure you that these efforts will be successful or produce our anticipated results.
Even where our R&D efforts are technically successful, we may not be able to apply the
technologies we developed to introduce new products on the expected timeline, or at all, due to lengthy
and uncertain development cycles. Delays, cost overruns or program cancellations could erode any first-
mover advantages, cause us to miss design windows, or allow competitors to secure design-ins with
alternative solutions. There can be no assurance that our R&D projects will yield the expected outcomes
or be completed within anticipated timelines and budgets.
If our R&D projects fail to achieve commercialization, the related expenditures would in effect
become sunk costs that may adversely affect our profitability and cash flows. In addition, resources such
as capital, R&D capacity and management attention devoted to such projects may limit our ability to
pursue alternative initiatives with clearer commercial visibility, thereby resulting in opportunity costs.
Even if the newly-developed products can be launched as expected, there can be no assurance that they
will be accepted by our customers or achieve the anticipated sales volumes or profitability. A portion of
our R&D expenses is directed to foundational technologies rather than specific products. While such
investment is important for long-term innovation and capability building, it may not immediately
enhance the competitiveness of our products in the market or generate the expected benefits or returns in
the short term. Furthermore, there can be no assurance that our existing or potential competitors will not
develop products that are technologically similar or superior to ours or are priced more competitively, in
which case we may lose market share. Given the uncertainties in the time frame for developing new
products and the duration of market windows for these products, there is also a risk that we may have to
discontinue the development of products that are no longer commercially viable, even after significant
resources have already been invested.

and our plans to expand our international operations have placed, and will continue to place, a strain on
our employees, management systems and other resources.

commercial risks. These include higher costs of understanding local markets and maintaining effective
marketing, distribution and customer support, difficulties in recruiting, retaining and managing local

direct delivery with periodic settlement and VMI arrangements that require customer draw-down and

credit risk. Customers may delay payment beyond agreed terms, seek extended terms, defer
reconciliations under VMI, or dispute quantities, specifications or quality. Deterioration in customers’
liquidity or financial condition, such as, due to industry downturns or macroeconomic factors, may
further extend collection periods or result in defaults.
During the Track Record Period, our trade receivables turnover days were 148.1 days, 150.1 days
and 144.0 days in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. As of December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, our
trade and notes receivables amounted to RMB719.7 million, RMB840.3 million and RMB1,220.6
million, respectively. There can be no assurance that these balances will be collected in accordance with
agreed payment terms, or at all. Any significant delay or default could increase our days sales
outstanding, operating cash flows and working capital, and reduce financial resources available for our
planned operations and investments.
We recognize expected credit loss allowances based on aging analysis, customer credit profiles and
forward-looking information. These estimates involve judgment and may differ from actual losses. If
actual credit losses exceed our allowances, or if collections are materially delayed, we may incur higher
impairment charges, experience reduced operating cash flows and require additional financing, and our
business, financial condition and results of operations could be adversely affected.
If we do not keep pace with technological developments and evolving customer specifications in the
industries we serve, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially
and adversely affected.
The markets for our products are characterized by rapid technology advancement and continuous
updates in terms of product designs and production processes, particularly in AI servers or AI
infrastructure where our products are widely used. Our competitiveness depends on our ability to
maintain and enhance core capabilities, design and manufacture products that meet evolving customer
specifications, and anticipate and adapt to technological change quickly and cost-effectively.
We anticipate that maintaining our technological advancement may necessitate increased
investment, driven by our customers’ expectations for products that require more advanced or quicker
turnaround times. If we cannot secure the resources to adapt as rapidly as competitors, or fail to
implement new technologies on time, our production efficiency may decline, yields or quality may fall,
and unit costs may rise, which could lead customers to delay qualifications or choose alternative
suppliers.

Our production relies on the stable supply of principal inputs, including cemented-carbide rods and

consumables, film substrates such as grating-structured base films used in our functional film products,

Certain of our key raw materials have historically been subject to supply constraints or shortage
risks. During the Track Record Period, we experienced supply constraints affecting materials for our
functional film products. In particular, the affected key raw material was grating-structured base film.
Specifically, in 2025, temporary fluctuations and constraints in the supply of such grating-structured
base films, together with certain batches of raw materials from our suppliers failing to meet our quality
control requirements, affected our production scheduling and actual output of functional film materials.

Disruptions in the availability or timely delivery of materials, interruptions in logistics or

The delivery, installation, inspection and acceptance of certain products may take longer than
expected. Any delay could affect our revenue recognition, liquidity and results of operations.
We generally recognize revenue when control of goods is transferred to customers. For domestic
sales of tools and auxiliary materials (e.g., PCB drilling bits, milling cutters and related consumables),
this typically occurs upon delivery and customer acknowledgement; for exports, upon customs clearance
and delivery to the customer’s designated location. For VMI arrangements with certain strategic
customers, we recognize revenue upon the customer’s draw-down and periodic reconciliation.
For specialized equipment that we sell in smaller volumes, revenue recognition may require
evidence of delivery and customer acceptance. Any of the delivery, installation, inspection or acceptance
steps may be delayed by factors beyond our control-for example, customer site readiness, scheduling
constraints, utilities access, or logistics-and there is no assurance that completion will occur by the
contractual deadline. Under our VMI model, revenue is recognized upon the customer’s draw-down and
periodic reconciliation. Until then, goods placed at customer sites remain on our books as inventory or
‘‘goods dispatched’’ and cannot be invoiced. Any delays in acceptance or reconciliation may defer
billing and cash collection, increase balances of trade receivables, which in turn raise/increase our
working capital requirements. If deliveries, installation, inspection or acceptance are delayed, or if
customers dispute specifications or timelines, our revenue recognition may be postponed, our inventory
and receivables may increase, and our cash flows and results of operations may be adversely affected.
There can be no assurance that such delays will not occur or that contractual penalties or other adverse
consequences will not arise.
Our product pricing is substantially influenced by prevailing market prices; adverse pricing trends
could negatively affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Prices for our PCB drilling tools, materials and intelligent CNC equipment are largely driven by

specifications) could compress margins. If market prices decline, or if price competition intensifies,
faster than we can reduce our costs or enhance product value, our revenue, gross margin and results of
operations could be adversely affected.

In addition to direct sales, we sell certain of our products through agents in selected regions and

direct sales by providing local coverage, customer liaison and limited after-sales coordination. During

sales volumes, tighter margins, longer cash-conversion cycles or inventory imbalances.

Our sales may be influenced by seasonality.
A significant portion of our revenue comes from products used in AI and high-performance
computing applications, which are generally less sensitive to seasonal trends. We also generate revenue
from products used in smart devices. Demand for smart devices is seasonal and can influence customers’
purchases of our PCB drilling tools, auxiliary materials and related equipment. Historically, we tend to
see higher sales in the second half of the year, driven by holiday-season shopping and product-launch
cycles. As a result, sales, working capital and operating cash flows are exposed to seasonal fluctuations,
and our quarterly or half-year results may not be indicative of full-year performance.
If we fail to maintain adequate inventory, or if we mismanage our inventory, we could lose sales or
incur higher inventory-related expenses and face inventory obsolescence, which could adversely
affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Our inventories mainly comprise raw materials, work in progress and finished goods. As of
December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025 our inventories were RMB339.8 million, RMB389.1 million and
RMB580.0 million, respectively. During the Track Record Period, our inventory turnover days were
141.8 days, 131.2 days and 142.5 days, respectively. Our business requires disciplined inventory
management across raw materials, work in progress and finished goods.
We depend on our demand forecasts to make purchase decisions for raw materials and
consumables and to pace our production progress to manage our inventories. Such demand, however,
can change from time to time and we may not always be able to accurately make predictions. Demand
may be affected by general market conditions, end market conditions, new product launches, pricing and
discounts, and not all of them are within our control. In addition, as we develop and market a new
product, we may not be successful in establishing stable and favorable supplier relationships or
accurately forecasting demand. The acquisition of certain types of raw materials and consumables may
require certain lead time and pre-payment and they may not be returnable. Furthermore, as we plan to
continue expanding our product offerings, we expect to include a wider variety of raw materials and
consumables, which will make it more challenging for us to manage our inventory and logistics
effectively.
We cannot assure you that inventory levels will swiftly meet customer demand, which may affect
revenue. Nor can we assure you that all inventory will be sold within a reasonable period. Poor
inventory management may lead to higher storage costs, slow-moving or obsolete stock and valuation
declines. It may also increase the likelihood of product obsolescence or force us to take write-offs, any
of which could materially and adversely affect our results and financial condition. Conversely, if we
underestimate demand or suppliers fail to deliver on time, stock-outs may occur, leading to lost orders
and customer churn, which could also harm our business, financial condition and results of operations.

We are subject to risks relating to third-party payments.
During the Track Record Period, there were limited instances where certain customers (the
‘‘Relevant Customers’’) settled amounts due to us through third parties designated by them (the
‘‘Third-Party Payors’’) who were not parties to the underlying sales and purchase agreements (the
‘‘Third-Party Payment Arrangements’’). The Third-Party Payors were primarily the legal
representatives or the business partners. To our knowledge, these arrangements arose mainly because
certain Relevant Customers operated on a small scale or as sole proprietorships and found it more
convenient to use such third-party accounts.
In one instance, on October 30, 2024, an Iran customer (the ‘‘Iran Customer’’) paid RMB18,959
to us through a third-party payor in China nominated by the Iran Customer. On October 29, 2024,
Nanyang Dtech, the Iran Customer and the third-party payor entered into a tripartite agreement, pursuant
to which the third-party payor remitted the payment to us in satisfaction of the Iran Customer’s payment
obligation, and any subsequent financial settlement between the third-party payor and the Iran Customer
was agreed to be handled separately. We believe that the third-party payor acted merely as a remittance
channel and that this arrangement constituted a Third-Party Payment Arrangement. In addition, the
aggregate transaction amounts settled via Third-Party Payment Arrangements, including the foregoing
arrangement, represented less than 0.01% of our total revenue in 2023, 2024 and 2025. For further
details, please refer to ‘‘Business — Sales and Marketing — Third Party Payment Arrangement.’’
However, we cannot assure you that risks will not materialize in the future. We may be exposed to

and other government grants, recognized in other income) of RMB41.3 million, RMB19.1 million and

Technology Enterprises (HNTE) and are therefore entitled to a preferential 15% income tax rate. We

enterprise income tax rate on taxable income. We cannot guarantee that we will receive such
government grants and preferential tax treatment in the future, and our financial condition and results of
operations may be adversely affected if we fail to obtain such government grants in the future.
RISKS RELATING TO DOING BUSINESS IN THE JURISDICTIONS WHERE WE OPERATE
Changes in economic, political and social conditions could materially and adversely affect our
prospects, business, results of operations and financial condition.
We derive revenue from, and conduct operations primarily in, the PRC, and we sell precision
cutting tools, grinding and polishing materials, functional film materials, and intelligent CNC equipment
to PCB manufacturers and other industrial customers. As such, changes in the economic, political and
social conditions in the jurisdictions where we operate and sell, could have a material and adverse
impact on our future prospects, business, results of operations and financial condition. Accordingly, our
future prospects, business, results of operations and financial condition are, to a material extent, subject
to macroeconomic, policy and legal developments in the jurisdictions where we operate. If the
macroeconomic environment experiences significant adverse changes, demand from downstream
electronics and industrial end-markets may weaken, our customers may reduce or defer capital
expenditure or consumables procurement, and our production and supply chain may face disruptions,
which could have a material and adverse impact on our business, results of operations and financial
condition.
Moreover, if foreign governments implement or expand laws, regulations or policies restricting
investment in, or transactions with, PRC-related entities and we are deemed to be subject to such
restrictions, investment in and transactions involving our Shares, as well as our business prospects,
results of operations, financial condition and future capital-raising activities, could be adversely affected.
Developments in the overseas legal systems of certain geographic markets where we operate may
affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

regions. The legal systems of these markets differ significantly, and many laws relevant to our business,

customs and export controls, cybersecurity and data protection, and labor and social security, have been

We are a Chinese Mainland enterprise and are subject to PRC tax on our global income. Any
gains on the sale of, and dividends on, our H Shares may be subject to PRC taxes.
Under the PRC EIT Law and its implementation rules, subject to any applicable tax treaty or
similar arrangement between Chinese Mainland and a non-Chinese Mainland investor’s jurisdiction of
residence that provides for a different income tax arrangement, Chinese Mainland withholding tax at the
rate of 10% is normally applicable to dividends from Chinese Mainland sources payable to investors that
are non-Chinese Mainland resident enterprises which do not have an establishment or place of business
in Chinese Mainland, or which have an establishment or place of business in Chinese Mainland but the
relevant income is not effectively connected with such establishment or place of business. Any gains
realized on the transfer of Shares by such investors are subject to a 10% Chinese Mainland income tax
rate if such gains are regarded as income from sources within Chinese Mainland unless a treaty or
similar arrangement provides otherwise.
Under the PRC Individual Income Tax Law and its implementation rules, dividends from sources
within Chinese Mainland paid to foreign individual investors who are not Chinese Mainland residents
are generally subject to a 20% Chinese Mainland withholding tax rate, and gains from Chinese Mainland
sources realized by such investors on the transfer of shares are generally subject to a 20% Chinese
Mainland income tax rate, in each case, subject to any reduction or exemption under applicable tax
treaties and laws in Chinese Mainland. Pursuant to the Notice on the Issues Concerning Individual
Income Tax Collection and Management after the Repeal of Guo Shui Fa [1993] No. 045 (Guo Shui
Han [2011] No. 348) dated June 28, 2011, issued by the SAT, dividends paid to non-Chinese Mainland
resident individual holders of H Shares are generally subject to the individual income tax of Chinese
Mainland at withholding tax rate of 10%, depending on whether there are tax arrangements between the
jurisdictions where the individual holders reside, as well as the tax arrangements between Chinese
Mainland and Hong Kong. Non-Chinese Mainland resident individual holders who reside in jurisdictions
that have not entered into tax treaties with Chinese Mainland are subject to a 20% withholding tax on
dividends received from us.
If Chinese Mainland income tax is imposed on gains realized from the transfer of our H Shares or
on dividends paid to our non-Chinese Mainland resident investors, the value of your investment in our
H Shares may be affected. Furthermore, our Shareholders whose jurisdictions of residence have tax
treaties or arrangements with Chinese Mainland may not qualify for benefits under such tax treaties or
arrangements.

The characteristics of the A share and H share markets may differ.
Our A Shares are listed and traded on the ChiNext of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. Following the
Global Offering, our A Shares will continue to be traded on the ChiNext of the Shenzhen Stock
Exchange and our H Shares will be traded on the Main Board of the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong.
Under current PRC laws and regulations, without approval from the relevant regulatory authorities, our
H Shares and A Shares are neither interchangeable nor fungible, and there is no direct trading or
settlement between the H share and A share markets.
Given different trading characteristics, the H share and A share markets have different trading
volumes, liquidity and investor bases, as well as different levels of retail and institutional participation.
As a result, the trading performance of our H Shares and A Shares may not be comparable. Fluctuations
in the price of our A Shares may adversely affect the price of our H Shares, and vice versa. Due to the
different characteristics of these markets, the historical prices of our A Shares may not be indicative of
the performance of our H Shares. You should not place undue reliance on the trading history of our A
Shares when evaluating an investment in our H Shares.
There has been no prior public market for our H Shares, and an active trading market for our H
Shares may not develop or be sustained.
Prior to the Global Offering, there was no public market for our H Shares. We cannot assure you
that a public market for our H Shares with adequate liquidity and trading volume will develop or be
sustained following the completion of the Global Offering. The Offer Price of our H Shares is expected
to be fixed by agreement between the Joint Sponsor-Overall Coordinators (for themselves and on behalf
of other Overall Coordinators and the Underwriters) and us, and may not be indicative of the market
price at which our H Shares will trade after the Global Offering. If an active public market for our H
Shares does not develop or is not sustained, the market price and liquidity of our H Shares may be
materially and adversely affected.

losses to investors.

performance of any particular company. The business performance and share price movements of other

WAIVERS FROM STRICT COMPLIANCE WITH THE LISTING RULES
In preparation for the Global Offering, our Company has sought the following waivers from strict
compliance with the relevant provisions of the Listing Rules, the SFO and the Companies (Winding Up
and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance:
MANAGEMENT PRESENCE IN HONG KONG
Pursuant to Rule 8.12 of the Listing Rules, we must have sufficient management presence in Hong
Kong. This normally means that at least two of our executive Directors must be ordinarily resident in
Hong Kong. Pursuant to Rule 19A.15 of the Listing Rules, the requirement in Rule 8.12 of the Listing
Rules may be waived by having regard to, among other considerations, our arrangements for maintaining
regular communication with the Stock Exchange.
Since the business operations of our Group are managed and conducted outside of Hong Kong, and
all of the executive Directors of our Company ordinarily reside outside Hong Kong, our Company
considers that it would be practically difficult and commercially unreasonable and undesirable for our
Company to arrange for two executive Directors to be ordinarily resident in Hong Kong, either by
means of relocation of existing executive Directors or appointment of additional executive Directors.
Therefore, our Company does not have, and does not contemplate in the foreseeable future that we will
have sufficient management presence in Hong Kong for the purpose of satisfying the requirements under
Rule 8.12 of the Listing Rules.
Accordingly, we have applied for, and the Stock Exchange has granted, a waiver from strict
compliance with Rule 8.12 and Rule 19A.15 of the Listing Rules, subject to the following conditions.
We will ensure that there is an effective channel of communication between us and the Stock Exchange
by way of the following arrangements:
. Authorized representatives: we have appointed Ms. WANG Xin and Ms. YE Jiahong as the
authorized representatives (‘‘Authorized Representatives’’) for the purpose of Rule 3.05 of
the Listing Rules. The Authorized Representatives will act as our principal channel of
communication with the Stock Exchange and would be readily contactable by phone,
facsimile and email to deal promptly with enquiries from the Stock Exchange. Accordingly,
the Authorized Representatives will be able to meet with the relevant members of the Stock
Exchange to discuss any matters in relation to our Company within a reasonable period of
time. The Company will also inform the Stock Exchange promptly in respect of any change
in the Authorized Representatives. See ‘‘Directors and Senior Management’’ for more
information about our Authorized Representatives;
. Joint company secretaries: in addition to the appointment of the Authorized Representatives,
Ms. YE Jiahong, one of our joint company secretaries and a Hong Kong resident, will,
among other things, act as our Company’s additional channel of communication with the
Stock Exchange and be able to answer enquiries from the Stock Exchange. Ms. YE Jiahong
will maintain contact with our Directors and senior management through various means,
including regular meetings and telephone discussions whenever necessary;
. Directors: to facilitate communication with the Stock Exchange, we have provided the
Authorized Representatives and the Stock Exchange with the contact details (such as mobile
phone numbers, office phone numbers, facsimile number and e-mail addresses, to the extent
possible) of each of our Directors such that the Authorized Representatives would have the

wishes to contact our Directors on any matters. In the event that any Director expects to

experience as required under Rule 3.28 of the Listing Rules and to become familiar with the

Our Company will further ensure that Ms. ZHOU Wenying has access to the relevant training and
support that would enhance his understanding of the Listing Rules and the duties of a company secretary
of an issuer listed on the Stock Exchange, and to receive updates on the latest changes to the applicable
Hong Kong laws, regulations and the Listing Rules. Prior to the end of the three-year period, the
qualifications and experience of Ms. ZHOU Wenying and the need for on-going assistance of Ms. YE

Rule 10.04 of the Listing Rules requires that a person who is an existing shareholder of the issuer
may only subscribe for or purchase any securities for which listing is sought which are being marketed
by or on behalf of the issuer either in his or its own name or through nominees if the conditions in
Rules 10.03(1) and (2) of the Listing Rules are fulfilled. It is provided in Rule 10.03(1) of the Listing
Rules that no securities may be offered to existing shareholders on a preferential basis and no
preferential treatment may be given to them in the allocation of the securities; and in Rule 10.03(2) that
the minimum prescribed percentage of public shareholders required by Rule 8.08(1) must be achieved.
Paragraph 1C(2) of Appendix F1 to the Listing Rules provides that no allocations will be permitted
to the existing shareholders of the applicant or their close associates, whether in their own names or
through nominees, in the Global Offering unless the conditions set out in Rules 10.03 and 10.04 of the
Listing Rules are fulfilled. Chapter 4.15 of the Guide provides that the Stock Exchange will consider
giving consent and granting waiver from Rule 10.04 of the Listing Rules to an applicant’s existing
shareholders or their close associates to participate in an initial public offering if any actual or perceived
preferential treatment arising from their ability to influence the applicant during the allocation process
can be addressed.

to ‘‘connected clients’’ of the overall coordinator(s), any syndicate member(s) (other than the overall

of the Stock Exchange.
Chapter 4.15 of the Guide for New Listing Applicants provides that the Stock Exchange will
ordinarily give its consent for allocation to connected clients if it is satisfied that: (i) the allocation to a
connected client represents genuine demand for securities of an applicant; and (ii) the connected client
has not taken and will not take advantage of its position to receive an allocation for its own benefit at
the expense of other placees or the public (i.e. no actual or perceived preferential treatment has been
given to such connected client).

OVERVIEW OF PRECISION CUTTING TOOL INDUSTRY
Definition and Classification of Precision Cutting Tools
The precision cutting tools industry serves as a fundamental support sector for mechanical
manufacturing, providing products essential for cutting, drilling, milling, and other machining processes.
By processing type, precision cutting tools can be classified into hole-processing tools, milling cutters,
turning tools, forming tools, etc. From the perspective of downstream applications, precision cutting
tools are used across PCB and precision component manufacturing, automotive production, general
– 79 –

=== PAGE 90 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
machinery, aerospace, construction machinery, and others. Within the PCB and precision component
manufacturing segment, key products include PCB cutting tools and CNC tools. PCB cutting tools are
specifically designed for precision operations such as drilling, milling, and cutting of PCBs. CNC tools,
on the other hand, are designed for automated, high-precision cutting in conjunction with CNC
machines.
Background of PCB Industry
Definition and Classification of PCB
The PCB is a foundational component in electronic equipment, providing the physical base for
mounting and electrically connecting electronic components. It features a predefined pattern of
conductive pathways on an insulating substrate, earning it the title of the foundation of the electronics
industry. PCBs are critical in a wide range of applications, including consumer electronics,
communication base stations, servers, automotive electronics, and many other fields. Based on product
type, PCBs can be classified into single and double-sided PCBs, multilayer boards, HDI boards, FPC,
and IC substrates. Multilayer PCBs (4 layers and above) contain multiple conductive layers, enabling
more components to be integrated within a limited space and thereby supporting enhanced functionality.
Within this category, the high-layer-count PCBs (8 layers and above) are particularly important in high-
performance applications like servers, network switches, and 5G base stations due to their advantages in
high-speed signal transmission, high integration, and reliability.
Market Size of PCB Industry
The global PCB market, measured by sales revenue, grew from US$76.9 billion in 2021 to
US$84.0 billion in 2025, representing a CAGR of 2.3% during this period. The overall market
contraction observed in 2023 was primarily attributable to a combination of factors, including weakened
demand for consumer electronics, inventory accumulation across the supply chain, and downward
pressure on average selling prices, with persistent softness in traditional segments like personal
computers, smartphones, and televisions. Looking ahead, advancements in global AI, data centers, next-
generation communication technologies, autonomous driving, and AR/VR are expected to underpin
steady market expansion. Projections indicate that the global PCB market is expected to have stable
growth from 2026 to 2030, with an anticipated CAGR of approximately 5.3%.

Market Drivers and Development Trends of PCB Industry
Emerging Technology Applications. The global PCB industry is entering a growth cycle fueled by
the adoption of emerging technologies, with core momentum stemming from explosive demand in key
frontier areas such as AI, high-performance computing, intelligent electric vehicles, and next-generation
communication technologies. In the realm of computing infrastructure, the rapid development of AI
servers significantly boosts demand for high-layer-count PCBs, thereby driving comprehensive
– 81 –

=== PAGE 92 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
advancements in PCB materials and processes. Furthermore, the ongoing R&D and deployment of 5G/
6G networks, the electrification and Intelligent trends in automotive electronics, the rapid proliferation
of AI-enabled endpoint devices (such as AI PCs and AI smartphones), and the continuous emergence of
new application scenarios like the low-altitude economy (e.g., drones), satellite internet, and industrial
internet collectively provide diversified long-term growth momentum for the PCB industry.
High Performance Technological Evolution. The global PCB industry is accelerating its evolution
towards high performance and high density. To meet the demands of end applications such as servers
and communication equipment for high-speed, high-frequency data processing and stable operation,
PCBs must adopt designs featuring higher layer counts, shorter trace lengths, and lower impedance. This
is achieved through material innovations and process optimizations. In addition, the global PCB industry
is evolving toward higher density, primarily driven by the trend of consumer electronics becoming
increasingly miniaturized and multifunctional. To accommodate greater functional integration within
limited space, the market is demanding finer via diameters, narrower trace widths, and higher layer
counts in PCBs.
Favorable Policy Support. Governments globally recognize the PCB industry as a core component
of the electronics manufacturing sector and are promoting its development through financial support, tax
incentives, and industrial chain integration. For instance, in U.S., the use of the Defense Production Act
(DPA) to allocate $50 million aims to support the U.S. PCB and advanced chip packaging industries.
Thailand’s Board of Investment has announced incentives to cover the entire supply chain of PCB.
Related companies would be eligible for up to eight years of corporate income tax exemption,
exemption from import duties on machinery, exemption from import duties on raw materials used in
production for export, and other non-tax incentives. China’s Printed Circuit Board Industry Specification
Conditions (2025 Edition)(Draft for Comments) emphasizes the need to improve product quality and
production efficiency while reducing production costs. China’s recommendations for the formulation of
the 15th Five-Year Plan emphasize accelerating innovation in digital and intelligent technologies,
strengthening the efficient supply of computing power, algorithms, and data, and promoting the
development of strategic emerging industry clusters, including new energy, advanced materials,
aerospace, and the low-altitude economy. This will directly boost demand for PCBs as a core electronic
component and promote breakthroughs in high-end technologies within the Chinese PCB industry.
Definition and Classification of PCB Cutting Tools
PCB cutting tools are specialized implements used in the manufacturing process of printed circuit
boards for key operations such as drilling, profiling, and surface treatment. Their performance directly
impacts the precision, reliability, and production efficiency of the final PCB products, making them
essential consumables in the electronics information industry. Classified by primary function, PCB
cutting tools can be categorized into drill bits, milling cutters, and specific-PCB tools.
. Drill Bits. Drill bits are used to create micro-holes — including through-holes, blind vias,
and buried vias — in the PCB substrate to establish electrical connectivity between different
layers. The drilling process is a critical step in PCB fabrication, as it directly affects the
board’s conductivity and signal integrity. By coating, drill bits include coated drills, which
feature a high-performance film applied to a carbide substrate to enhance performance, and
uncoated drills, which have no additional coating material on the base substrate.
. Milling Cutters. Milling cutters, or end mills, are used for surface milling, cutting, and
shaping of the PCB, such as creating planes, steps, and grooves. Common types include
diamond-type, chip-breaking type, continuous-edge type, and two-flute type end mills, among
others.
– 82 –

=== PAGE 93 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
. Specific-PCB Tools. This category encompasses tools designed for specific processing
requirements. Examples include two-flute routing tools for thick copper and aluminum-based
boards, beveling tools for processing gold finger interfaces, chamfering tools for internal
groove or screw hole chamfering, engraving tools for blind slots or fine engraving, and V-
groove tools for V-scoring.
Industry Chain of PCB Cutting Tools
The PCB cutting tool industry has established a complete ecosystem spanning from raw material
supply to end-user applications, with its upstream, midstream, and downstream sectors working in close
synergy to support the high-precision processing demands of the electronics manufacturing industry. The
upstream sector forms the foundation of the industry, primarily supplying high-performance raw
materials and specialized equipment. The midstream sector is responsible for transforming these
upstream materials into high-precision cutting tools, with its product range primarily consisting of drill
bits and milling cutters. The downstream sector, centered on PCB manufacturing, represents the core
source of demand. Its terminal applications cover servers, communications equipment, consumer
electronics, automotive electronics etc..

high-performance servers can be further categorized into AI servers and general-purpose servers.

differentiated technical requirements on drill bit specifications. Drill bit requirements vary significantly
across three major application segments: standard PCBs, high-layer-count PCBs and HDI boards, and IC

Analysis of China’s PCB Drill Bits Market
As the world’s largest PCB manufacturing hub, China benefits from a highly concentrated and
integrated industry ecosystem, which provides a strong and stable demand base for the PCB drill bits
market. China’s PCB drill bit market grew from RMB2.5 billion in 2021 to RMB3.8 billion in 2025,
representing a CAGR of 10.6% during this period, outpacing the growth rate of the global market.
China’s share of the global PCB drill bit market increasing from 61.6% to 63.0% over the same period.
This growth was primarily driven by the expansion of China’s PCB market. In 2021, China’s PCB
market size accounted for 54.2% of the global market, a proportion which increased to 57.5% in 2025.
China’s PCB industrial clustering allows PCB drill bit manufacturers to work closely with
downstream PCB producers throughout the entire production cycle, from collaborative product
development to large-scale manufacturing, enabling faster response to evolving technical requirements.
This has fueled a distinct market trend in China towards rapid technological advancement and sustained
capacity expansion in drill bits, driven by the well-established PCB industry ecosystem compared to the
global market. China’s PCB drill bit market is projected to reach RMB6.3 billion by 2030, with its share
of the global PCB drill bit market increasing further to 63.5%.
Analysis of Coated PCB Drill Bits Market
Based on whether the product surface has additional coating materials, the global market share of
coated drill bits was 35.4% in 2025. High-end applications such as AI servers, 5G communications, and
automotive electronics are driving the development of PCBs towards higher density and more layers,
resulting in harder substrate materials, denser circuits, and a significant increase in the number of holes
drilled. This imposes stringent requirements on the wear resistance, precision, and heat resistance of drill
bits. Coated drill bits, which utilize coating materials such as TiCN or diamond, can significantly
enhance the hardness of the drill bit and reduce friction loss, offering a longer service life compared to
uncoated drills. This effectively ensures the processing yield and efficiency of high-end PCBs and
reduces the cost per hole drilled. As a result, the global market share of coated drills is expected to
continue rising, reaching 51.6% by 2030.
Market Drivers of PCB Drill Bits Industry
The Iteration PCB Products is Driving the Evolution of Drill Bits Towards Higher-end
Specifications. The rapid development of cutting-edge fields such as AI and autonomous driving is
accelerating the evolution of PCBs towards higher layer counts and high-density interconnects. The
trend toward higher-density PCBs has increased the number of holes per unit area while reducing hole
diameters. The higher layer count results in deeper drilling depths. These technological shifts are driving
increased demand for high precision micro drills, high aspect ratio drills, and coated drill bits. In
addition, drill bits with a high aspect ratio are more prone to breakage and deviation during the
machining process, therefore, PCB manufacturers tend to reduce the hole limit (the allowable number of
uses per drill bit) to mitigate the risk of drill breakage, degraded hole-wall quality, or even full-board
scrap. This practice directly results in a significant increase in drill bit consumption.
The Iteration of Substrate Materials Compels Upgrades in Drill Bits. The evolution of PCB
substrates toward high-frequency, high-speed, and composite materials directly forces innovation in drill
bit materials and processes. The widespread application of high-frequency materials and metal
substrates, which exhibit high hardness and strong thermal conductivity, poses severe challenges to
conventional drill bits, significantly accelerating wear. In this context, advanced coating technology is
regarded as a key pathway to enhance wear resistance, extend service life, and reduce overall costs.
Consequently, the ongoing iteration of PCB substrates further drives the expansion of the coated drill bit
market.
