Development Trends of PCB Drill Bits Industry
Accelerated Domestic Substitution and Deepened Global Layout. The Chinese PCB drill bit
industry is exhibiting two core development trends: the acceleration of domestic substitution and the
deepening of global layout. Domestic enterprises, leveraging continuous technological innovation and
significant cost-performance advantages, are increasingly enhancing their competitiveness in the global
market. They are gradually substituting imported products and production equipment, and actively
exploring overseas markets. The Southeast Asia region has become a key area for production capacity
layout due to its industrial supporting facilities and cost advantages.
The Adoption of Intelligent Management Systems Has Become Increasingly Widespread. With
the widespread adoption of intelligent manufacturing concepts and technologies in China, PCB
manufacturers are placing greater demands on the digital management of production processes, tools,
supply chains, and product quality. For example, intelligent drill management systems can track the
complete usage history and regrinding cycles of each drill bit through dedicated chips embedded in the
tools, enabling full lifecycle management — from storage and allocation to return and regrinding.
The Rapid Expansion of the PCB Market is Driving Capacity Upgrades Across the Drill Bit
Industry. Accelerating PCB demand — particularly the shift toward higher layer counts and greater
density — is directly increasing drill bit consumption and placing higher requirements on manufacturers’
capacity expansion capabilities. To address this demand, leading companies are building competitive
advantages by independently developing and manufacturing core production equipment, thereby
enhancing flexibility in scaling output and improving responsiveness to market needs. At the same time,
ongoing process innovation and the integration of automated production systems are enabling
manufacturers to further improve efficiency and yield, supporting the industry’s robust growth trajectory.
Raw Material Price Analysis of PCB Drill Bits Industry
Tungsten powder and cobalt are the core raw materials for PCB drill bits. Tungsten powder is first
carbonized and then mixed with cobalt powder as a binder according to a specific formulation to
produce high-hardness, wear-resistant tungsten rods, which serve as the primary raw material for
manufacturing PCB drill bits. Consequently, fluctuations in tungsten and cobalt prices have a significant
impact on overall production costs and profitability in the PCB drill bit market.
From 2021 to 2025, the price of tungsten in China showed a steady upward trend. The prices of
tungsten powder increased from RMB238/kg in 2021 to RMB491/kg in 2025. Among this period, the
most notable increase occurred in 2025. This significant increase was primarily attributable to the
implementation of stringent total production control measures on tungsten mining by the Chinese
government. These regulatory constraints limited upstream supply, resulting in a corresponding increase
in prices. Cobalt prices rose from RMB379,157/ton in 2021 to RMB427,777/ton in 2022 before
gradually declining to RMB199,302/ton in 2024, and then increased to RMB320,517/ton in 2025. From
2021 to 2022, cobalt prices experienced a moderate increase, primarily driven by growing demand from
the electric vehicle sector and concurrent supply chain constraints. Between 2022 and 2024, prices
declined as newly released production capacity in regions such as Indonesia led to an increase in global
supply. From 2024 to 2025, cobalt prices rebounded, mainly due to export restrictions and the
implementation of a quota system by the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which resulted in a modest
contraction in supply, resulting in a corresponding increase in prices. These fluctuations are mainly
driven by supply-demand dynamics, economic conditions, and policy factors.

Entry Barriers of PCB Drill Bits Industry
Technology Barrier. The production of PCB drill bits involves precision manufacturing and
materials science, demanding high technical expertise that is difficult for new entrants to master in the
short term. Leading companies have accumulated a strong patent advantage through long-term R&D
investment, covering areas such as micro-drill design, coating technology, and automated equipment,
thereby constructing significant technological barriers.
Stringent Customer Certification Systems. Downstream PCB manufacturers impose relatively
strict certification requirements on their suppliers, making it difficult for new companies to quickly
secure orders. The certification process includes qualification reviews, sample testing, small-batch trials,
and large-scale validation, all of which require considerable time to complete. PCB manufacturers tend
to form long-term, stable strategic partnerships with qualified drill bit suppliers, and customer loyalty
strengthens as the cooperation continues. Consequently, it is challenging for new enterprises to rapidly
establish collaborative relationships with PCB manufacturers.
Supply Chain and Cost-Control Capabilities. Effective supply chain management and cost control
are crucial for maintaining competitiveness. The core raw materials for PCB drill bits rely on high-
quality suppliers, and leading companies typically establish long-term, stable cooperative relationships
with their primary suppliers. New entrants face difficulties in obtaining competitive procurement prices.
Besides, leading enterprises continuously reduce production costs through large-scale production, refined
management, and process optimization, giving them a more competitive unit price. New companies
generally face procurement and cost disadvantages.
Capital Barriers. The PCB drill bit industry is characterized by significant capital intensity.
Substantial upfront investment is required for production line construction, posing a primary challenge
for new entrants. In addition, some of the core production equipment for high-end drill bits is heavily
reliant on imports, and these machines are expensive, further increasing initial investment and
operational costs. This creates significant financial barriers for new entrants in the industry.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Definition and Classification of CNC Tools
CNC tools generally refer to tools used for cutting and machining in industrial machinery
manufacturing processes. To ensure the stable operation and maximize the performance of CNC machine
tools, they must be equipped with cutting tools suited to their operating conditions and machining
environment. The design, manufacturing, and application requirements of CNC tools are higher than
those of conventional tools, with key differences in precision, structure, materials, and coating treatment.
Based on main machining process, CNC tools can be categorized into turning tools, drilling tools and
milling cutters.
Market Size of CNC Tools
In terms of sales revenue, the China’s CNC tool market expanded from RMB38.7 billion in 2021
to RMB57.5 billion in 2025, with a CAGR of 10.4% during this period. Moving forward, automotive
sector expansion boosts demand for CNC tools, supported by the warming up of the electric vehicle
market. Hence, China’s CNC tool market is expected to reach RMB89.8 billion in 2030, with a CAGR
of 8.8% from 2026 to 2030.
Market Drivers and Development Trends of CNC Tool Industry
Demand-Side Drivers. Demand from automotive, aerospace, electronics, machinery, and energy
sectors is pushing manufacturers to order higher-precision, more flexible CNC machines-machines
capable of multi-axis operations, higher spindle speeds, and tighter tolerances. This downstream demand
is especially visible in the automotive and electronics industries, where small, complex parts must meet
exacting surface finish and geometry standards, driving the need for adaptive machining and real-time
monitoring systems.
Product and Technology Innovation. Advances in AI, machine learning, multi-axis machining,
hybrid manufacturing, and real-time monitoring are accelerating improvements in productivity,
precision, and automation. Companies are adopting hybrid manufacturing techniques that blend
subtractive CNC machining with additive steps to reduce material waste and offer more complex
geometries. Also, innovations in simulation and optimization software are enabling manufacturers to test
tool paths virtually before production, improving tool life and reducing error rates.
OVERVIEW OF GRINDING AND POLISHING MATERIALS INDUSTRY
Definition and Classification of Grinding and Polishing Materials
Grinding and polishing materials are a general term for industrial materials used for grinding, wire
drawing, and polishing workpiece surfaces. Their core function is to remove surface imperfections,
burrs, and reduce roughness through physical or chemical action, thereby achieving a smooth, flat
surface or one with a specific luster. These materials typically possess high hardness, toughness, and a
regular shape. They are widely used in the precision processing of materials such as glass, metal, plastic,
semiconductors, and gemstones, serving as key consumables in the manufacturing industry for
enhancing both the esthetic quality and functional performance of products. Classified by form and
function, grinding and polishing materials can be divided into two major categories: grinding tools and
grinding grains.
Grinding tools are instruments formed by bonding grinding grains together with a bonding agent
(such as brush grinding wheels, grinding wheels, grinding belts, flap wheels, sponge wheels, cloth
wheels, etc.), which are used for direct contact with the workpiece to perform grinding, lapping, or
polishing operations. Grinding grains refer to the granular materials that perform the cutting action (such
as aluminum oxide, silicon carbide, diamond, etc.), which remove irregularities from the workpiece
surface through friction.

=== PAGE 101 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Market Drivers and Development Trends of Grinding and Polishing Materials
Diversified Expansion of Downstream Application Fields. The growth in demand for grinding and
polishing materials benefits significantly from the continuous broadening and deepening of their
downstream applications. With the advancement of high-end manufacturing and the emergence of new
industries — particularly in semiconductors, precision optics, aerospace, and biomedical sectors — the
demand for components with higher geometric precision, smoother surfaces, and greater reliability has
steadily increased, driving the high-quality development of the grinding and polishing materials
industry.
Material Innovation and Upgrade. Continuous technological and process advancements serve as
the core internal drivers of market development. Nanomaterials demonstrate superior performance in
precision polishing, significantly reducing surface roughness. At the same time, against the backdrop of
China’s dual-carbon targets and the green transformation of manufacturing, environmental standards are
becoming increasingly stringent. As a result, the demand for eco-friendly materials is steadily rising,
aligning with policy-driven initiatives promoting green manufacturing.
OVERVIEW OF FUNCTIONAL FILM MATERIALS INDUSTRY
Overview of Functional Film Materials
Functional film materials are advanced polymer-based composite films that exhibit engineered
optical, electrical, and physical properties such as light modulation, heat insulation, privacy protection,
and surface enhancement. These films serve as key components enabling smart, energy-efficient, and
human-centric display and glass systems across both the automotive and consumer electronics sectors.
The industry has evolved from early-stage decorative and protective films to today’s highly
functional optical films integrated with sensors, coatings, and intelligent control modules. By
manipulating light transmission, reflection, and absorption at the microscopic level, these materials
allow dynamic adjustment of visibility, brightness, and color tone, thereby enhancing user experience
while improving energy efficiency and device durability. From the demand side, the applications of
functional films are primarily concentrated in the automotive, consumer electronics, building materials,
semiconductor manufacturing, and new energy sectors:
. Automotive Light-control Functional Films. Applied in car sunroofs, side windows,
windshields, and central display screens, improving driving comfort and energy efficiency
through dimming, anti-glare, and heat insulation technologies. In China, the market size of
automotive light-control functional films for central displays grew from RMB1.1 billion in
2021 to RMB3.1 billion in 2025 achieving a CAGR of 30.0% over the period. Looking
ahead, the market is projected to reach RMB6.5 billion by 2030, reflecting a CAGR of 14.9%
from 2026.
. Consumer Electronics Functional Films. Used in smartphones, tablets, laptops, and other
devices to provide privacy protection, blue-light filtering, anti-reflection, and anti-fingerprint
performance, meeting user needs for privacy, safety, and visual health. In 2024, the market
size of consumer electronics functional films in China reached RMB53.4 billion.
. Other Functional Films. In building materials, functional film materials are primarily used
for decoration and protection to enhance wear resistance, stability, and environmental
performance; in semiconductor manufacturing, functional film materials are applied in
lithography, cleaning, and packaging processes to ensure precise fabrication and high yield
rates; in the new energy sector, functional film materials are mainly used in lithium-ion
battery separators and photovoltaic encapsulation films, providing critical support for battery
safety, energy density, and the long-term durability of PV modules.

OVERVIEW OF INTELLIGENT CNC EQUIPMENT AND PRECISION COMPONENTS
INDUSTRY
Overview of the Intelligent CNC Equipment and Precision Components Industry
Intelligent CNC equipment integrates multiple technologies, has sensing-decision-execution loops,
and features automation, digitalization, and connectivity. It drives manufacturing intelligence upgrades
and boosts productivity. Precision components are high-accuracy parts in various systems, serving high-
end manufacturing. The intelligent CNC equipment and precision components industry is a core pillar of
China’s high-end manufacturing. Precision components support intelligent CNC equipment, and the
latter enables production automation, digitalization, and intelligence, enhancing efficiency. Their
coordinated development drives key technological breakthroughs, accelerates the shift to intelligent
production, and lays a foundation for industrial upgrading and global competitiveness. The CNC
equipment and precision components industry is experiencing significant growth driven by the
continuous upgrading of downstream demand. As industries such as automotive, aerospace, electronics,
and machinery manufacturing evolve, the need for higher precision, better efficiency, and advanced
automation has become increasingly critical.
Definition and Classification of CNC Grinding Machines
A CNC machinery tool is a type of the CNC equipment. It has numerical control systems to
automatically execute machining processes according to digital programs. CNC grinding machines
represent an important sub-segment within the CNC machine tool industry. They use a CNC system to
drive the relative motion between the grinding tool and the workpiece according to preset programs for
high-precision automated grinding. As an important part of the industrial backbone machine ecosystem,
they are essential for precision manufacturing of various materials and complex components with
extensive adoption across various manufacturing sectors. Based on workpiece geometry, they can be
classified into external cylindrical, internal cylindrical, coordinate, centerless, surface, belt, honing, and
lapping grinders, with external cylindrical, internal cylindrical, and surface grinders being most widely
used.
Definition and Classification of Precision Components
Precision components refer to key fundamental elements in mechanical, electronic, optical, and
other systems that undertake precise transmission, positioning, measurement, or control functions. They
typically feature high precision, high reliability, and high consistency, serving as the core foundation for
the stable operation and performance enhancement of intelligent CNC equipment. Different application
scenarios impose varying requirements on their performance and process characteristics.
Outlook Analysis of the Embodied Robotics Market
Embodied intelligence, as an emerging field, works in synergy with intelligent CNC equipment to
promote the intelligent transformation of manufacturing. Embodied intelligence refers to an intelligent
system based on physical bodies for perception and action. Through the interaction between the agent
and its environment, it gathers information, understands problems, makes decisions, and carries out
actions, resulting in intelligent behavior and adaptability. Humanoid robots are one of the typical
implementations of embodied intelligence. Equipped with perception devices such as vision and touch,
they have decision-making capabilities and perform diverse tasks in real-world environments using
actuators like mechanical arms or wheeled and tracked drives. The embodied robotics market in China is
experiencing a rapid expansion, with the market size expected to grow from RMB3.8 billion in 2025 to
RMB54.5 billion in 2030, with a CAGR of 70.6%. Embodied robotics, driven by large models, will
accelerate the development of general intelligence, promote human-machine collaboration, and industrial
upgrading, becoming the core engine that connects the physical world with digital intelligence.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
APPLICABLE LAWS AND REGULATIONS OF CHINA BUSINESS
Laws and regulations relating to companies
According to the Company Law of the People’s Republic of China (the ‘‘Company Law’’), revised
by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (the ‘‘NPC Standing Committee’’) on
December 29, 2023 and effective from July 1, 2024, companies are generally divided into two
categories: limited liability companies and joint stock limited companies. The Company Law also
applies to foreign-invested enterprises, but where laws on foreign investment provide otherwise, those
provisions shall prevail.
Regulations and policies relating to the industry
From 2009 to 2021, the State Council issued a series of regulations aiming at promoting the
development of printed circuit board industry, including the Electronic Information Industry Adjustment
and Revitalization Plan, the Notice of the State Council on Issuing the National Strategic Emerging
Industries Development Plan for the 13th Five-Year Plan, and the Notice of the State Council on Issuing
the Digital Economy Development Plan for the 14th Five-Year Plan. On February 27, 2023, the Central
Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council issued the Overall Layout Plan for
the Construction of Digital China.
The Regulatory Conditions for the Printed Circuit Board Industry and the Interim Measures for the
Administration of Public Announcements on Printed Circuit Board Industry Standards, promulgated and
effective on February 1, 2019 by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (‘‘MIIT’’),
established a quantitative standard system for printed circuit board enterprises and projects from multiple
dimensions, including capacity layout and project construction, production scale and process technology,
intelligent manufacturing, green manufacturing, safe production, social responsibility, and other
dimensions.
The Catalog of Industries for Encouraging Foreign Investment (2022 Version) (the ‘‘Encouraging
Catalog’’), promulgated by the NDRC and the MOFCOM on October 26, 2022 and effective from
January 1, 2023, explicitly includes ‘‘high-density interconnect laminated boards, single-layer, double-
layer and multi-layer flexible boards, rigid-flex printed circuit boards and package substrates, high-
density fine-line flexible circuit boards (line width/spacing ≤0.05 mm)’’ in the scope of industries
encouraged for foreign investment. On December 20, 2024, the NDRC and the MOFCOM promulgated
the revised Catalog of Industries for Encouraging Foreign Investment (Draft for Public Comment),
which still includes the above industries in the scope of industries encouraging foreign investment.
According to the Catalog for Guiding Industrial Structure Adjustment (2024 Edition) issued by the
NDRC on December 27, 2023 and effective on February 1, 2024, printed circuit boards, special
equipment for the production of electronic components, and functional film materials are encouraged
industries.
Regulations concerning companies and foreign investment
Enterprise entities established and operating in China are governed by the Company Law. The
Company Law of China primarily regulates two types of companies: limited liability companies and
joint stock limited companies.
On January 1, 2020, the Law of the People’s Republic of China on Foreign Investment (the
‘‘Foreign Investment Law’’) and the Regulations for the Implementation of the Foreign Investment
Law of the People’s Republic of China came into effect. The Foreign Investment Law sets out the
definition of foreign investment and the framework for promoting, protecting, and managing foreign
investment activities. On December 30, 2019, the MOFCOM and the State Administration for Market
Regulation (‘‘SAMR’’) jointly promulgated the Measures for the Reporting of Information on Foreign
Investment (which became effective on January 1, 2020). According to these Measures, foreign investors
– 93 –

=== PAGE 104 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
establishing foreign-invested enterprises and establishing foreign-invested enterprises by acquiring
equity in non-foreign-invested enterprises, as well as subsequent changes, must submit an initial or
change report to the enterprise registration system.
Pursuant to the Foreign Investment Law, China has adopted a system of national treatment which
includes a negative list with respect to foreign investment administration. The negative list will be
issued by, amended or released upon approval by the State Council, from time to time. The negative list
will set forth industries in which foreign investments are prohibited and industries in which foreign
investments are restricted. Foreign investment in prohibited industries is not allowed, while foreign
investment in restricted industries must satisfy certain conditions stipulated in the negative list. Except
for the scope of prohibited and restricted industries stipulated in the negative list, foreign investment and
domestic investment in other industries will be treated equally. The Special Administrative Measures for
Foreign Investment Access (Negative List) (2024 Edition) (the ‘‘Negative List’’), promulgated by the
NDRC and the MOFCOM on September 6, 2024 and effective on November 1, 2024, and the
Encouraged Industry Catalog, promulgated by the NDRC and the MOFCOM on October 26, 2022 and
effective on January 1, 2023, list the categories of encouraged, restricted, and prohibited industries. Any
industry not included in the Negative List shall be administered under the principle of equal treatment to
domestic and foreign investment.
Regulations on customs declaration
The Customs Law of the People’s Republic of China, most recently revised by the Standing
Committee and effective on April 29, 2021, stipulates that China Customs is the government agency
responsible for supervising and controlling all entries into and exits from customs territories. All means
of transport, goods and articles must enter or leave the territory of China through places where customs
are established. The consignor or consignee of import and export goods, or a customs declaration
enterprise entrusted by the relevant consignor or consignee, may handle customs declaration and tax
payment procedures. Consignees and consignors of import and export goods and customs brokers shall
register with the Customs when handling customs declaration procedures, otherwise they may be fined
by the Customs.
According to the Regulations of the People’s Republic of China on the Administration of Customs
Declaration Entities Filing, promulgated by the General Administration of Customs of China (‘‘GACC’’)
on November 19, 2021 and effective on January 1, 2022, consignees and consignors of import and
export goods and customs declaration enterprises applying for customs filing shall obtain the
qualification of market entities; among them, consignees and consignors of import and export goods
applying for customs filing shall also obtain the filing of foreign trade operators. In addition, the
Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on Amending the Foreign Trade
Law of the People’s Republic of China, promulgated by the Standing Committee of the National
People’s Congress on December 30, 2022 and effective on the same day, removed the requirement that
foreign trade operators engaged in the import and export of goods or technology should register with the
administrative department in charge of foreign trade under the State Council or any institution entrusted
by it.
In accordance with the Regulations of the People’s Republic of China on the Administration of
Import and Export of Goods (the ‘‘Regulations on the Administration of Import and Export of
Goods’’), promulgated by the State Council on December 10, 2001, most recently revised on March 10,
2024, and effective on May 1, 2024, enterprises engaging in trade activities involving the import of
goods into or the export of goods out of the People’s Republic of China must comply with the
Regulations on the Administration of Import and Export of Goods.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Regulations on safe production, fire safety, and product quality
Regulations on production safety
According to the Production Safety Law of the People’s Republic of China (the Production Safety
Law), most recently revised by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on June 10,
2021 and effective from September 1, 2021, entities engaged in production and business activities in
Chinese Mainland must comply with the Production Safety Law and other relevant laws and regulations
on production safety. Entities shall strengthen the management of production safety, establish and
improve safety production responsibility systems and safety production rules and regulations, improve
safety production conditions, strengthen the standardization and informatization of safety production,
and enhance the level of safety production to ensure production safety.
Regulations on fire safety
The Fire Protection Law of the People’s Republic of China was most recently revised by the
Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on April 29, 2021, effective on the same day.
The Interim Provisions on the Administration of Fire Protection Design Review and Acceptance of
Construction Projects was most recently revised by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural
Development of the People’s Republic of China (‘‘MOHURD’’) on August 21, 2023, effective on
October 30, 2023. In accordance with the above laws and regulations, for construction projects that are
required to apply for fire acceptance as stipulated by the competent department of housing and urban-
rural development under the State Council, the construction entity shall apply to the competent
department of housing and urban-rural development for fire acceptance upon completion of the project.
For other construction projects not specified in the preceding paragraph, the construction entity shall file
with the housing and urban-rural development authority after acceptance.
Regulations on product quality
The Civil Code of the People’s Republic of China (the ‘‘Civil Code’’) was promulgated by the
National People’s Congress of the People’s Republic of China on May 28, 2020 and came into effect on
January 1, 2021. Pursuant to the Civil Code, manufacturers shall assume tort liability where the defects
in relevant products cause damage to others.
In accordance with the Product Quality Law of the People’s Republic of China, most recently
revised by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on December 29, 2018 and
effective on the same day, producers shall be responsible for the quality of the products they produce,
and the quality of products shall meet the following requirements: (i) not having unreasonable threats to
personal and property safety, and conforming to national standards or industry standards for ensuring
human health, personal safety and property safety, where such standards exist; (ii) possessing the
performance properties that the product should have, except where there are explanations about the
functional defects of the product; and (iii) conforming to the product standards indicated on the product
or its packaging, and to the quality conditions indicated by way of product instructions, physical
samples, and other means.
Environmental Protection Regulations
The Environmental Protection Law of the People’s Republic of China was most recently revised by
the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on April 24, 2014 and effective on January
1, 2015. According to the Environmental Impact Assessment Law of the People’s Republic of China,
most recently revised by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on December 29,
2018 and effective on the same day, the Regulations on Environmental Protection Management of
Construction Projects, most recently revised by the State Council on July 16, 2017 and effective on
October 1, 2017, and the Interim Measures for the Environmental Protection Acceptance of Completed
Construction Projects, promulgated by the former Ministry of Environmental Protection on November

=== PAGE 106 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
20, 2017 and effective on the same day, China implements an environmental impact assessment system
for construction projects. The construction unit shall submit an environmental impact report or an
environmental impact statement for approval before the commencement of the construction project, or
file an environmental impact registration form in accordance with the regulations of the environmental
protection administrative department of the State Council. In addition, after the completion of
construction projects for which environmental impact reports or environmental impact registration forms
have been prepared, the construction unit shall, in accordance with the standards and procedures
stipulated by the environmental protection administrative department of the State Council, conduct
acceptance inspections of the environmental protection facilities built in conjunction with the projects
and prepare acceptance reports. The environmental protection facilities supporting the construction
project can only be put into production or use after passing the acceptance inspection; those that have
not been inspected or have failed the inspection shall not be put into production or use.
Regulations on air pollution
According to the Law of the People’s Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of
Atmospheric Pollution, which was most recently revised by the Standing Committee of the National
People’s Congress on October 26, 2018 and came into effect on the same day, enterprises, public
institutions, and other producers and operators shall monitor their discharged industrial waste gas or
toxic and harmful atmospheric pollutants listed in the catalog specified in Article 78 of the Law of the
People’s Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Atmospheric Pollution, in accordance with
relevant state regulations and monitoring standards, and shall keep original monitoring records.
Enterprises, public institutions, and other entities subject to pollution discharge permit management in
accordance with the law, that discharge industrial waste gasses or toxic and hazardous air pollutants
listed in the aforementioned catalog, shall obtain a pollution discharge permit. In addition, enterprises,
public institutions and other producers and operators constructing projects that may affect the
atmospheric environment shall conduct environmental impact assessments and disclose environmental
impact assessment documents in accordance with the law.
Regulations on solid waste
According to the Law of the People’s Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of
Environmental Pollution Caused by Solid Wastes, which was last amended by the Standing Committee
of the National People’s Congress on April 29, 2020 and came into effect on 1 September 2020, any
entity or individual that generates, collects, stores, transports, utilizes, or disposes of solid waste shall
take measures to prevent or reduce environmental pollution caused by solid waste, and shall be liable for
resultant environmental pollution in accordance with the law. If solid waste contains hazardous waste, it
should be managed in accordance with the hazardous waste management measures.
Regulations concerning water pollution
According to the Water Pollution Prevention and Control Law of the People’s Republic of China,
which was last amended by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on June 27, 2017
and came into effect on January 1, 2018, enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and
operators that directly or indirectly discharge industrial wastewater, medical sewage, or other wastewater
and sewage that require a pollutant discharge permit into water bodies, shall obtain a pollutant discharge
permit.
Regulations on pollutant discharge
According to the Regulations on the Administration of Permitting of Pollutant Discharges
promulgated by the State Council on January 24, 2021 and effective on March 1, 2021, and the Catalog
for the Classified Management of Pollutant Discharge Permitting for Stationary Pollution Sources (2019
Edition) promulgated by the Ministry of Ecology and Environment on December 20, 2019 and effective

on the same date, enterprises, public institutions and other producers and operators that are subject to
pollutant discharge permit management as stipulated by laws must apply for and obtain pollutant
discharge permits; without this permit, discharging pollutants is prohibited.
Laws and regulations concerning real estate, planning and construction
The Land Administration Law of the People’s Republic of China (the ‘‘Land Administration
Law’’) was most recently revised by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on
August 26, 2019 and became effective on January 1, 2020. Pursuant to the Land Administration Law,
construction entities that have obtained state-owned land use rights through paid leasing must pay the
land use right leasing fees and other fees and expenses in accordance with the standards and methods
prescribed by the State Council before they can use the land. The Interim Regulations on Immovable
Property Registration, most recently revised by the State Council on March 10, 2024 and effective on
May 1, 2024, and the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Interim Regulations on Immovable
Property Registration, most recently revised by the Ministry of Natural Resources on May 9, 2024 and
effective on the same day, stipulate (among other things) that the State implements a unified immovable
property registration system.
The Provisional Regulations of the People’s Republic of China on Assignment and Transfer of
Urban State-owned Land Use Rights was first promulgated by the State Council on May 19, 1990 and
implemented after the latest revision on November 29, 2020. According to these regulations, land users
shall develop, utilize and manage the land in accordance with the provisions of the contract for the
assignment of land use right and the requirements of urban planning. If the land is not developed and
used within the period and conditions as stipulated in the contract, the land administration departments
under the people’s governments at the municipal and county levels shall rectify the situation and may
impose penalties, including warnings, fines or the uncompensated reclamation of land use rights,
depending on the circumstances.
According to the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國城鄉規劃法》) most
recently revised by the SCNPC on April 23, 2019 and became effective on the same day, if the
construction of buildings, structures, roads, pipelines and other projects is carried out in the planned
area of a city or a town, the construction entity or individual shall apply to the competent authority of
urban and rural planning of the people’s government of the city or county or the people’s government of
the town as determined by the people’s government of the province, autonomous region or municipality
directly under the Central Government for a construction project planning permit.
According to the Regulations on the Administration of Construction Project Quality, promulgated
and implemented by the State Council on January 30, 2000 and revised on April 23, 2019, if a
construction unit commences construction without obtaining a construction permit or without approval
of the commencement report, it shall be ordered to cease construction, rectify within a specified period,
and be subject to a fine of between 1% and 2% of the project contract price.
Regulations on housing lease management
Pursuant to (i) the Law on Administration of Urban Real Estate of the People’s Republic of China,
most recently revised by the SCNPC on August 26, 2019 and took effect on January 1, 2020, and (ii)
the Administrative Measures on Leasing of Commodity Housing, promulgated by the Ministry of
Housing and Urban-Rural Development on December 1, 2010 and came into effect on February 1, 2011,
when leasing premises, the lessor and lessee are required to enter into a written lease contract,
containing such provisions as the leasing term, use of the premises, rental and repair responsibility, and
other rights and obligations of both parties. Both the lessor and the lessee shall, within 30 days after
signing the property lease contract, register and file the property lease with the property management
department at the location of the leased property. If the lessor and lessee fail to complete the registration
and filing procedures, both the lessor and lessee may be subject to fines.

According to the Civil Code, a lease contract is a contract under which the lessor delivers to the

Laws and Regulations on Intellectual Property in China
Patent
The Patent Law of the People’s Republic of China was most recently revised by the Standing
Committee of the National People’s Congress on October 17, 2020 and effective on June 1, 2021. The
Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People’s Republic of China was most recently
revised by the State Council on December 11, 2023 and effective on January 20, 2024. According to
these laws, regulations and implementing rules, Chinese patents are divided into three categories:
invention patents, utility model patents and design patents. The term of an invention patent right is 20
years, the term of a utility model patent right is 10 years, and the term of a design patent right is 15
years, all calculated from the date of application. Any entity or individual exploiting another person’s
patent shall conclude a license agreement with the patentee and pay a patent exploitation fee to the
patentee. Implementing a patent without the patentee’s permission constitutes an infringement of their
patent rights.
Trademark
The Trademark Law of the People’s Republic of China was most recently revised by the Standing
Committee of the National People’s Congress on April 23, 2019 and came into effect on November 1,
2019; the Regulations for the Implementation of the Trademark Law of the People’s Republic of China
was most recently revised by the State Council on April 29, 2014 and came into effect on May 1, 2014.
Pursuant to these laws and regulations, the validity period of a registered trademark is 10 years,
commencing from the date of approval of registration. If the registered trademark needs to be
continuously used after the expiration of its validity period, renewal procedures shall be handled in
accordance with regulations within 12 months before its expiration.
Domain name
The Administrative Measures for Internet Domain Names were promulgated by the MIIT on
August 24, 2017 and became effective on November 1, 2017. According to administrative measures, the
MIIT is the primary regulatory authority responsible for the administration of PRC internet domain
names. Domain name registration is processed through domain name root servers, domain name root
server operating organizations, domain name registration authorities, and domain name registration
service organizations established in accordance with relevant regulations.
Computer Software Copyright
The Measures for the Registration of Copyright in Computer Software, promulgated by the
National Copyright Administration on February 20, 2002 and effective on the same day, regulate the
registration of copyright in computer software, exclusive licensing contracts and transfer contracts for
copyright in computer software. The National Copyright Administration is mainly responsible for the
administration of software copyright registration nationwide, and designates the China Copyright
Protection Center as the agent for software registration. The China Copyright Protection Center will
issue registration certificates to applicants for computer software copyrights.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Laws and Regulations on Anti-Monopoly and Anti-Unfair Competition
Pursuant to the Anti-Monopoly Law of the People’s Republic of China (the ‘‘Anti-Monopoly
Law’’), most recently revised by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on June 24,
2022 and effective on August 1, 2022, the Anti-Monopoly Law applies to monopolistic practices in
economic activities within China, as well as monopolistic practices outside China that have the effect of
eliminating or restricting competition in the domestic market. The monopolistic practices under the Anti-
Monopoly Law include any monopoly agreement reached by any operators, abuse of market-dominating
position by any operators and any concentration of operators which has eliminated or limited or may
eliminate or limit the market competition. Where an operator violates the provisions of the Anti-
Monopoly Law, the anti-monopoly enforcement agency shall order it to cease the illegal act and may
impose a fine.
According to the Anti-unfair Competition Law of the People’s Republic of China (the ‘‘Anti-
unfair Competition Law’’) most recently revised by the Standing Committee of the National People’s
Congress on June 27, 2025 and implemented on October 15, 2025, operators shall abide by the
principles of voluntariness, equality, fairness, and integrity, as well as laws and business ethics in
market transactions.
Regulations on labor and social welfare
Labor
The Labor Law of the People’s Republic of China was most recently revised by the Standing
Committee of the National People’s Congress on December 29, 2018 and came into effect on the same
day. The Labor Law of the People’s Republic of China stipulates matters concerning employment
promotion, labor contracts, working hours, rest and leave, wages, labor safety and hygiene, special
protection for female employees and juvenile workers, vocational training, social insurance and welfare,
labor disputes, supervision and inspection, and legal liabilities.
The Labor Contract Law of the People’s Republic of China was most recently revised by the
Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on December 28, 2012, coming into effect on
July 1, 2013; the Regulations on the Implementation of the Labor Contract Law of the People’s Republic
of China were promulgated by the State Council on September 18, 2008 and came into effect on the
same day. According to the above laws and regulations, a written labor contract shall be concluded to
establish an employment relationship. Employers shall not compel employees to work overtime.
According to the Supreme People’s Court’s Interpretation (II) on Several Issues Concerning the
Application of Law in Labor Dispute Cases《( 最高人民法院關於審理勞動爭議案件適用法律問題的解
釋(二)》) (the ‘‘New Judicial Interpretation’’), which was promulgated by the PRC Supreme People’s
Court on 31 July 2025 and came into effect on 1 September 2025, Article 19(1) stipulates that where an
employer and an employee agree, or the employee undertakes, that social insurance contributions need
not be paid, the People’s Court shall deem such agreement or undertaking invalid. Furthermore, where
an employer fails to pay social insurance contributions in accordance with the law and the employee
seeks to terminate the labor contract and claim economic compensation pursuant to Article 38(3) of the
PRC Labor Contract Law, the People’s Court shall support such claims in accordance with the law.
According to the Interim Provisions on Labor Dispatch promulgated by the Ministry of Human
Resources and Social Security and came into effect on March 1, 2014, the number of dispatched workers
hired by an employer may not exceed 10% of the total number of its employees. Where rectification is
not made within the stipulated period, the employers may be subject to a penalty ranging from
HK$5,000 to HK$10,000 per dispatched worker exceeding the 10% threshold.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Social insurance
The Social Insurance Law of the People’s Republic of China (the ‘‘Social Insurance Law’’), most
recently revised by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on December 29, 2018
and effective on the same day, establishes social insurance systems including basic endowment
insurance, basic medical insurance, work-related injury insurance, unemployment insurance and
maternity insurance, and details the legal obligations and liabilities of employers for non-compliance
with social insurance-related laws and regulations. According to the Social Insurance Law and the
Interim Regulations on the Collection of Social Insurance Premiums most recently revised by the State
Council on March 24, 2019 and effective on the same day, enterprises should register with the local
social insurance administration and pay or withhold relevant social insurance for their employees. If an
employer fails to pay social insurance, it shall be ordered to pay within a time limit, and a late payment
fine shall be imposed. If the employer still fails to rectify the failure to make social insurance
contributions within the stipulated deadline, it may be subject to a fine ranging from one to three times
the amount overdue.
Housing provident fund
According to the Regulations on the Management of Housing Provident Fund most recently revised
by the State Council on March 24, 2019 and effective on the same day, employers in Chinese Mainland
should provide housing provident funds for their employees. Where an employer fails to pay the
aforementioned housing provident fund, the housing provident fund management center may order it to
pay the full amount within a prescribed time limit. If an employing entity fails to pay the housing
provident fund within the prescribed time limit, an application may be made to the people’s court for
compulsory collection.
Regulations on overseas investment
According to the Administrative Measures for Overseas Investments of Enterprises promulgated by
the National Development and Reform Commission on December 26, 2017 and effective on March 1,
2018, investors engaging in overseas investments shall complete procedures such as approval and filing
of overseas investment projects, report relevant information, and cooperate with supervision and
inspection.
Pursuant to the Administrative Measures for Overseas Investment most recently revised by the
Ministry of Commerce on September 6, 2014 and effective on October 6, 2014, ‘‘overseas investment’’
refers to the acts of enterprises legally established in China to own non-financial enterprises or acquire
ownership, control, operation and management rights and other interests of existing non-financial
enterprises overseas through new establishment, mergers and acquisitions and other means. The Ministry
of Commerce and provincial commerce authorities implement filing and approval management
respectively, according to the actual circumstances of enterprises’ overseas investments. Overseas
investment involving any sensitive country or region or any sensitive industry shall be subject to
confirmation management. Overseas investments by enterprises under other circumstances shall be
subject to filing administration. If an overseas enterprise invested by an enterprise carries out overseas
reinvestment, the enterprise shall report to the competent commercial authority after completing the
overseas legal procedures.
In accordance with the ‘‘Provisions on Foreign Exchange Administration of Overseas Direct
Investment by Domestic Institutions’’ issued by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange of the
People’s Republic of China (‘‘SAFE’’) on July 13, 2009 and effective on August 1, 2009, and the
‘‘Notice on Further Simplifying and Improving Foreign Exchange Administration Policies for Direct
Investment’’ issued by SAFE on February 13, 2015, effective on June 1, 2015, and partially repealed on
December 30, 2019, after obtaining approval for relevant overseas investments, Chinese enterprises
making overseas direct investments shall apply to the bank in their place of registration for foreign
exchange registration.

Regulations on foreign exchange
In accordance with the Regulations of the People’s Republic of China on Foreign Exchange
Administration most recently revised by the State Council on August 5, 2008 and effective on the same
day, and the Administrative Provisions on Settlement, Sale and Payment of Foreign Exchange
promulgated by the People’s Bank of China on June 20, 1996, effective on July 1, 1996, Renminbi
conversion for current account items such as payment for trade, service-related foreign exchange
transactions, and dividend payments is unrestricted after relevant financial institutions conduct a
reasonable review of the authenticity of transaction documents and their consistency with foreign
exchange receipts and payments. However, Renminbi conversion for capital account items such as direct
investment, loans, or investment in securities outside China requires prior approval from the State
Administration of Foreign Exchange or its local branches.
According to the Notice of the People’s Bank of China and the State Administration of Foreign
Exchange on Issues Concerning the Management of Funds for Overseas Listing of Domestic Enterprises
issued by the People’s Bank of China and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange on December
24, 2025 and effective from April 1, 2026, domestic enterprises conducting overseas listings shall,
within 30 working days after the first trading day of the overseas listing or the completion of the over-
allotment, submit the required application materials to the bank in the province or city specifically
designated in the state plan where they are located to complete the overseas listing registration. In
principle, funds raised by domestic enterprises through overseas listings shall be remitted back to the
PRC in a timely manner. If such funds are retained outside the PRC for outbound direct investment,
outbound securities investment, outbound lending, or other related businesses, the domestic enterprise
shall obtain approval or filing documents from the competent authorities prior to the completion of the
offshore issuance or over-allotment, and shall comply with relevant cross-border fund management
regulations.
According to the Notice of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange on Reforming and
Standardizing the Foreign Exchange Settlement Management Policy of Capital Account, promulgated by
the State Administration of Foreign Exchange on June 9, 2016 and effective on the same day, and the
Circular of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange on Further Deepening Reforms to Facilitate
Cross-border Trade and Investment, promulgated by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange on
December 4, 2023 and effective on the same day, domestic institutions’ capital account foreign
exchange revenue is subject to the voluntary foreign exchange settlement policy.
According to the Guidelines on Foreign Exchange Business under the Capital Account (2024
Edition) issued by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange on April 3, 2024 and effective on May
6, 2024, which stipulate regulatory requirements for securities investment management and other related
foreign exchange business, operational guidance is provided on foreign exchange procedures for new
registration and alteration and cancellation of registration, registration of domestic shareholders’
shareholdings and other related matters of domestic companies’ overseas listings.
Tax laws and regulations
Enterprise income tax
According to the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People’s Republic of China (the ‘‘Enterprise
Income Tax Law’’), promulgated by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on
March 16, 2007, most recently revised on December 29, 2018 and effective on the same day, a uniform
income tax rate of 25% shall apply to foreign-invested enterprises and foreign enterprises with
establishments or places of business in China, as well as Chinese enterprises. In accordance with the
Enterprise Income Tax Law, enterprises established outside China but whose ‘‘de facto management
body’’ is located within China are deemed ‘‘resident enterprises’’ and will generally be subject to
enterprise income tax at a uniform rate of 25% on their global revenue.

Value-added Tax
According to the ‘‘Notice of the Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration on
Adjusting VAT Rates’’ (Cai Shui [2018] No. 32) issued by the Ministry of Finance and the State
Taxation Administration on 4 April 2018 and effective on May 1, 2018, for VAT taxable sales or import
of goods by taxpayers, the original VAT rates of 17% and 11% shall be adjusted to 16% and 10%
respectively.
According to the Announcement on Policies Related to Deepening Value-Added Tax Reform
(Announcement No. 39 of 2019 by the Ministry of Finance, the State Administration of Taxation and
the General Administration of Customs) issued by the Ministry of Finance, the State Administration of
Taxation and the General Administration of Customs on March 20, 2019 and effective on April 1, 2019,
for taxpayers engaging in VAT taxable sales or importing goods, the applicable VAT rates of 16% and
10% have been adjusted to 13% and 9% respectively.
According to the Value-Added Tax Law of the People’s Republic of China promulgated by the
Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on December 25, 2024, entities and individuals
selling goods, services, intangible assets, or real estate within China, as well as importing goods, shall
pay value-added tax. The applicable VAT rates for general taxpayers are 13%, 9%, 6% and 0%, while
the collection rate for entities using the simplified taxation method is 3%.
Dividend tax
Pursuant to the Individual Income Tax Law of the People’s Republic of China (the ‘‘Individual
Income Tax Law’’), as most recently amended by the Standing Committee of the National People’s
Congress on August 31, 2018 and effective from January 1, 2019, and the Regulations for the
Implementation of the Individual Income Tax Law of the People’s Republic of China (the
‘‘Implementation Regulations of the Individual Income Tax Law’’), as most recently amended by the
State Council on December 18, 2018 and effective from January 1, 2019, Chinese companies generally
withhold income tax at a uniform rate of 20% on dividends distributed to individual investors.
Meanwhile, according to the Notice on Issues Concerning Differentiated Individual Income Tax Policies
on Dividends and Bonuses of Listed Companies issued by the Ministry of Finance, the State
Administration of Taxation, and the China Securities Regulatory Commission on September 7, 2015 and
effective on September 8, 2015, individual income tax shall be temporarily exempted on dividends and
bonuses obtained by individuals from listed company shares acquired through public offerings, if the
shareholding period exceeds one year and the shares are transferred in the stock market. For individuals
who acquire shares of listed companies through public offerings or transfer shares of listed companies in
the stock market, if the shareholding period is within one month (including one month), the entire
dividend income shall be included in the taxable income; if the shareholding period is more than one
month to one year (including one year), 50% of the dividend income shall be included in the taxable
income; the aforementioned income shall be subject to individual income tax at a uniform rate of 20%.
Pursuant to the Arrangement between the Mainland and the Hong Kong Special Administrative
Region on the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion, which became
effective on August 21, 2006, the Chinese Government may levy taxes on the dividends paid by a
Chinese company to Hong Kong residents (including natural persons and legal entities), but the tax
amount shall not exceed 10% of the total dividends payable. If a Hong Kong resident directly holds 25%

Regulations on Securities and Overseas Listing
Securities laws and regulations
The Securities Law of the People’s Republic of China (the ‘‘Securities Law’’), promulgated by the

related guidelines, which became effective on March 31, 2023. According to the Administrative
