Undeveloped Land Parcels in Xinye County
Pursuant to the agreement entered into between Nanyang Dtech and the local relevant authority
Nanyang Dtech was granted land use rights to three land parcels in Xinye County, with areas of
7,297.24 sq.m., 94,477.02 sq.m. and 5,679.60 sq.m., respectively, and was required to commence and
complete construction within the prescribed timeframes under the relevant contracts. As of the Latest
Practicable Date, construction on the First Land Parcel and the Third Land Parcel had not commenced,
primarily due to our construction planning and the fact that both parcels are hardened land requiring
additional preparation for construction. In respect of the Second Land Parcel, a building with a gross
floor area of 2,242.85 sq.m. had been constructed, but the area on which construction had commenced
accounted for less than one-third of the total construction land area on which development was required
to commence. Pursuant to the Measures for the Disposal of Idle Land (2012 Revision)《( 閒置土地處置
辦法(2012修訂)》), where construction has not commenced within one year from the agreed
commencement date, or where the developed area is less than one-third of the total area required to be
developed, the relevant land may be identified as idle land. In such circumstances, the competent
authority may impose a land idling fee equivalent to 20% of the land grant or allocation price if
construction has not commenced for more than one year, and may reclaim the relevant state-owned
construction land use right without compensation if construction has not commenced for two years.
During the Track Record Period, the Group had not been subject to any administrative penalties. In
addition, according to a certificate dated March 2, 2026 issued by the Xinye County Natural Resources
Bureau (the ‘‘Bureau’’), which, as advised by our PRC Legal Advisor, is the competent authority with
respect to the relevant land-use matters, Nanyang Dtech had lawfully used the relevant land in
compliance with applicable land-use laws and regulations, was not under investigation by, or subject to
any administrative penalties imposed by the Bureau, and the Bureau had no intention to reclaim any part
of the relevant state-owned construction land use rights currently held by Nanyang Dtech, nor had it
received any report from any third party alleging violations in respect of such land use.
In light of the foregoing, including (i) the certificate issued by the Bureau, (ii) the opinion of the
PRC Legal Advisor confirming that the risk of the Company simultaneously having the land reclaimed
and being subject to material administrative penalties is remote and (iii) the fact that the Group’s current
production scale can be supported by its existing operating sites and the new land parcels in Dongguan
on which the Group has already commenced construction of new production facilities, and that the

SEASONALITY
Our business may be affected by fluctuations in downstream end-market demand from time to
time. A significant portion of our revenue is derived from products used in AI and high-performance
computing applications, which are generally less sensitive to seasonal trends. We also generate revenue
from products used in smart devices, and demand for such end-products is typically stronger in the
second half of the year due to holiday-season consumer spending and product launch cycles. As a result,
demand from certain customers for our PCB drilling tools, auxiliary materials and related equipment
may also be relatively higher in the second half of the year. This may in turn affect purchases by certain
customers of our PCB drill bits, auxiliary materials and related equipment. For related risks, see ‘‘Risk
Factors — Our sales may be influenced by seasonality.’’

RISK MANAGEMENT AND INTERNAL CONTROL
We are exposed to various risks for our operations so risk management is important for our
business. For details of the various operational risks we face, please refer to the section headed ‘‘Risk
Factors’’ in this document. In addition, we are also exposed to different financial risks, such as liquidity,
credit and foreign exchange risks that arise in the ordinary course of our business. For details, please
refer to the paragraphs headed ‘‘Financial Information — Financial Risks Disclosure’’. In order to
identify, assess, control and monitor the risks that may cause impediments to our business, we have
designed and implemented policies and procedures to help ensure effective risk management in our
operations.
We have adopted a consolidated series of risk management policies which set out a risk
management framework to identify, assess, evaluate and monitor key risks associated with our strategic
objectives on an on-going basis. Our audit committee, and ultimately our Board supervises the
implementation of our risk management policies. Risks identified by senior management will be
analyzed on the basis of likelihood and influence, and will be properly followed up and mitigated and
rectified by our Company and reported to our Board.
Our senior management implements the risk management policies, strategies and plans set by our
Board. Each functional team monitors and evaluates the implementation of risk management and internal
control policies and procedures on a day-to-day basis. In order to formalize risk management among our
Company and set a standard level of transparency and risk management performance, the relevant teams
will (i) gather information of the risks relating to their operation or function; (ii) conduct risk
assessments, which include the identification, prioritization, categorization and measurement of all key
risks that could potentially affect their objectives; (iii) continuously monitor the key risks relating to
their operation or function; (iv) implement appropriate risk control actions when necessary; and (v)
develop and maintain an appropriate mechanism to facilitate the application of our risk management
framework.
With respect to urgent matters which arise between scheduled Board meetings, the Board secretary
may also seek Board approval via telephone conference call or written Board consent. Before each
Board meeting, an agenda is prepared with input from Directors, as well as from senior management. At
Board meetings, depending on the agenda, heads of different departments will gather information
relating to their functions and report to the Board on the relevant agenda items, as necessary. The Board
secretary attends all Board meetings to ensure that there is no gap in communication between the two
bodies. During Board meetings, the Board will on occasion further review and/or analyze particular
issues and report their findings at the next Board meeting. Our Board believes that our corporate
structure provides an appropriate system of checks and balances to improve our risk management
procedures.
Our audit committee also reviews and approves our risk management policy to ensure that it is
consistent with our corporate objectives, reviews and approves our corporate risk tolerance, monitors the
most crucial risks associated with our business operation and our management’s handling of such risks,
reviews our corporate risks in light of our corporate risk tolerance, and monitors and ensures the
appropriate application of our risk management framework among our Company.

Our Board is responsible for establishing our internal control system and reviewing its
effectiveness. During the Track Record Period, we regularly reviewed and enhanced our internal control
system. Below is a summary of the internal control policies, measures and procedures we have
implemented or plan to implement:
. We have adopted various measures and procedures regarding each aspect of our operations,
such as protection of intellectual property, environmental protection and occupational health
and safety. We provide periodic training on these measures and procedures to our employees

. Our Directors (who are responsible for monitoring the corporate governance of our Group)

. We have established the Audit Committee which shall (i) make recommendations to our

and payroll, taxation, insurance, IT general controls, and R&D and intellectual property management.
The Internal Control Consultant identified certain areas for improvement, primarily relating to the timely
updating of certain corporate governance policies for Listing Rules compliance, and the enhancement of

financial management.
We have implemented rectification and improvement measures, as the case may be, in response to
the Internal Control Consultant’s findings and recommendations, including:
. Corporate governance. We revised and enhanced our corporate governance policies and
procedures.
. Asset management. We enhanced our policies and procedures relating to fixed assets and
intangible assets.
. Insurance management. We established insurance management procedures and approved
relevant insurance arrangements.
. IT general controls. We enhanced our controls over system changes, data backup, user
access and software management.
. Financial and treasury management. We enhanced our policies and procedures relating to
financial reporting, treasury management and payables.

NON-COMPETITION AND CLEAR DELINEATION OF BUSINESS
Our Business
We are a leading integrated provider of precision manufacturing solutions, bringing together tools,
materials and intelligent equipment for key process segments of the global printed circuit board (PCB)
fabrication value chain, primarily including drilling, routing/forming and other related precision
manufacturing processes.
The Business of Our Controlling Shareholders
Taiding Holdings is an investment holding company incorporated under the laws of the PRC on
November 16, 2017. Zhejiang Taiding is a limited partnership established under the laws of the PRC on
July 10, 2018. Taizhou Ruihe serves as an employee shareholding platform of the Group with no actual
business operations. Apart from business of our Company, our group of Controlling Shareholders also
controls companies which engage in, among others, investment holdings, real estate development and
operation, manufacture and sale of liquor.
In light of the above, our Directors are of the view that there is a clear delineation between the
businesses operated by our Controlling Shareholders and our Group.

NON-COMPETE UNDERTAKINGS
In connection with the A-Shares Listing, Ms. WANG Xin, Mr. WANG Junfeng, Mr. WANG
Xuefeng, Mr. LIN Xia and Taiding Holdings have provided a non-compete undertaking dated June 22,
2021 (‘‘Non-compete Undertaking’’), which carries no expiry date, to our Company in order to avoid
potential competition, pursuant to which, Ms. WANG Xin, Mr. WANG Junfeng, Mr. WANG Xuefeng
and Mr. LIN Xia has undertaken that, among others:
(1) they will not, through any means (including but not limited to sole proprietorship, joint
venture or actual holding of equity interests in other company or enterprise), directly or
indirectly participate in or engage in business or projects identical or similar to the operation
business scope of the Company, nor establish, develop, participate in or assist any legal
entity or other economic organization either for themselves or on behalf of any third party in
direct or indirect competition with the Company. Neither themselves or any other enterprise
controlled by them shall, either directly or indirectly, within or outside the PRC, engage in
the research and development, production, or sale of any project or product that the Company
develops, produces or sells (including but not limited to projects or products for which the
Company has already invested research funds to develop or which are already in trial
production or which are already in formal production);
(2) they will not leverage their understanding of the Company and the information obtained to
directly or indirectly participate or engage in commercial activities that compete with the
Company and will not directly or indirectly participate or engage in any other competitive
conduct that harms or may harm the Company’s interests. Such competition includes but not
limited to directly or indirectly recruiting the Company’s technical personnel, sales personnel
or senior management, improperly utilizing the Company’s intangible assets, disparaging the
Company’s product image and corporate image in advertising or promotion;

Having considered the following factors, our Directors are satisfied that we are able to carry on
our business independently from our Controlling Shareholders and their respective close associates upon
completion of the Global Offering.
Management independence
Our business is managed and conducted by our Board and senior management. Upon the Listing,
our Board will consist of nine Directors, including five executive Directors and four independent non-
executive Directors. Ms. WANG Xin, Mr. WANG Junfeng, Mr. WANG Xuefeng and Mr. LIN Xia have
at all times devoted sufficient time and attention to the performance of their duties as Directors and have
consistently complied with the relevant provisions of laws, regulations and the Articles of Association.
In performing their duties as Directors, they have been and will continue to be supported by the Group’s
independent directors and senior management team. The operations of the senior management and the
Board ensure a balance of power and authority. For further details, please see the section headed
‘‘Directors and Senior Management’’ in this Prospectus.
Although Ms. WANG Xin, Mr. WANG Junfeng, Mr. WANG Xuefeng and Mr. LIN Xia are part of
the group of Controlling Shareholders, we consider that the Board and senior management will function
independently from the Controlling Shareholders for the following reasons:

represent a majority of the Board), along with Mr. XU Hui, Ms. ZHOU Wenying and Mr.

with the Controlling Shareholders and their respective close associates. They have substantial
experience in the industry as further described in the section headed ‘‘Directors and Senior
Management’’, which will enable them to discharge their duties independently from the
Controlling Shareholders;
(ii) each of our Director is aware of his/her fiduciary duties as a director which require, among
other things, that he/she acts for the benefit and in the interest of our Company and does not
allow any conflict between his/her duties as a Director and his/her personal interests;
(iii) we have appointed four independent non-executive Directors, comprising more than one-third
of the total members of our Board, who have sufficient knowledge, experience and
competence with a view to bring independent judgement to the decision-making process of
our Board;
(iv) we have adopted a series of corporate governance measures to manage conflicts of interest, if

governance measures’’ in this section; and

Based on the above, our Directors are satisfied that sufficient corporate governance measures have
been put in place to manage conflicts of interest between our Group and our Controlling Shareholders
and/or their respective close associates, and to protect minority Shareholders’ interests after the Global
Offering.

BOARD COMMITTEES
Our Board delegates certain responsibilities to various committees. In accordance with the relevant
PRC laws and regulations, the Corporate Governance Code and the Listing Rules, the Company has
established four committees under the Board of Directors, namely the Audit Committee, the
Remuneration and Appraisal Committee, the Nomination Committee, and Strategy Committee.
Audit Committee
We have established the Audit Committee in compliance with Rule 3.21 of the Listing Rules and
the Corporate Governance Code set out in Appendix C1 to the Listing Rules. The primary duties of the
Audit Committee are to review our Company’s financial information and its disclosure, supervise and
evaluate internal and external audit work and internal control, and to provide our Board with
professional advice. The Audit Committee comprises three independent non-executive Directors, namely,
Mr. SONG Haihai, Dr. XIN Guosheng and Ms. LI Xiaofei. Mr. SONG Haihai is the chairperson of the
Audit Committee. He holds the appropriate professional qualifications and as required under Rules
3.10(2) and 3.21 of the Listing Rules.
Remuneration and Appraisal Committee
We have established the Remuneration and Appraisal Committee in compliance with Rule 3.25 of
the Listing Rules and the Corporate Governance Code. The primary duties of the Remuneration and
Appraisal Committee are to formulate the appraisal standards for Directors and senior management,
conduct appraisal, and formulate and review the remuneration policies and proposals for Directors and
senior management. The Remuneration and Appraisal Committee comprises three Directors, namely, Ms.
LI Xiaofei, Mr. SONG Haihai and Ms. WANG Xin. Ms. LI Xiaofei is the chairperson of the
Remuneration and Appraisal Committee.
Nomination Committee
We have established the Nomination Committee in compliance with Rule 3.27A of the Listing
Rules and the Corporate Governance Code. The primary duties of the Nomination Committee are to
assess the candidates and review selection criteria and procedures for Directors and senior management,
and to make recommendations to the Board. The Nomination Committee comprises of three Directors,
namely, Dr. XIN Guosheng, Ms. LI Xiaofei and Mr. WANG Junfeng. Dr. XIN Guosheng is the
chairperson of the Nomination Committee.

Strategy Committee
We have established the Strategy Committee in compliance with the Articles of Association. The
primary duties of the Strategy Committee are to review our Company’s long-term development strategies
and major investment decisions, and to make recommendations to our Board. The Strategy Committee
comprises three Directors, namely, Ms. WANG Xin, Mr. LIN Xia and Mr. WANG Junfeng. Ms. WANG
Xin is the chairperson of the Strategy Committee.
BOARD DIVERSITY POLICY
The Board of Directors has adopted a board diversity policy (the ‘‘Board Diversity Policy’’) in
order to enhance the effectiveness of our Board of Directors and to maintain high standard of corporate
governance. The Board Diversity Policy sets out the criteria in selecting candidates to our Board of
Directors, including but not limited to gender, age, cultural and educational background, ethnicity,
professional experience, skills, knowledge and length of service. The ultimate decision will be based on
merit and contribution that the selected candidates will bring to our Board of Directors.
Our Directors have a balanced mixed of knowledge and skills, including but not limited to overall
business management, finance and accounting and material science. They obtained degrees in diversified
majors including economics, business administration, engineering, human resources management,
accounting and editing and publishing.
In addition, our Board of Directors has a wide range of age, ranging from 28 years old to 73 years
old. Two of our Directors is also female. Our Board is of the view that our Board of Directors satisfies
the Board Diversity Policy. Our Board will also ensure that appropriate balance of gender diversity is
achieved with reference to investors’ expectation, and international and local recommended best
practices.
The Nomination Committee is responsible for reviewing the diversity of our Board. After the
Listing, the Nomination Committee will monitor and evaluate the implementation of the Board Diversity
Policy from time to time to ensure its continued effectiveness. The Nomination Committee will also
include in successive annual reports a summary of the Board Diversity Policy, including any measurable
objectives set for implementing the Board Diversity Policy and the progress on achieving these
objectives.
CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
We recognize the importance of incorporating elements of good corporate governance in our
management structure and internal control procedures so as to achieve effective accountability. Our
Company intends to comply with all code provisions in the Part 2 of the Corporate Governance Code as
set out in Appendix C1 to the Listing Rules after the Listing apart from code provision C.2.1 of Part 2
of the Corporate Governance Code, which provides that the roles of chairperson of the Board and chief
executive should be separate and should not be performed by the same individual.
The roles of chairperson of the Board and general manager of our Company are currently
performed by Ms. WANG Xin. In view of Ms. WANG Xin’s substantial contribution to our Group since
our establishment and her extensive experience, we consider that having Ms. WANG Xin acting as both
our chairperson of the Board and general manager will ensure consistent leadership within our Group
and facilitate the efficient execution of our business strategies. We consider it appropriate and beneficial
to our business development and prospects that Ms. WANG Xin continues to act as both our chairperson
of the Board and general manager after the Listing, and therefore currently do not propose to separate
the functions of chairperson of the Board and general manager. While this would constitute a deviation
from code provision C.2.1 of Part 2 of the Corporate Governance Code, the Board believes that this
structure will not impair the balance of power and authority between the Board and the management of

Shares can be subscribed for and traded by mainland Chinese investors, qualified foreign institutional
investors or qualified foreign strategic investors and must be traded in Renminbi. As our A Shares are
eligible securities under the Northbound Trading Link, they can also be subscribed for and traded by
Hong Kong and other overseas investors pursuant to the rules and limits of Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock

2. RANKING
Our H Shares and our A Shares are regarded as one class of Shares under our Articles of
Association and will rank pari passu with each other in all other respects and, in particular, will rank
equally for all dividends or distributions declared, paid or made after the date of this Prospectus. All
dividends in respect of our H Shares are to be paid by us in Hong Kong dollars whereas all dividends in
respect of our A Shares are to be paid by us in RMB. In addition to cash, dividends may also be
distributed in the form of Shares. Holders of our H Shares will receive share dividends in the form of H
Shares, and holders of our A Shares will receive share dividends in the form of A Shares.
3. NO CONVERSION OF OUR A SHARES INTO H SHARES FOR LISTING AND TRADING
ON THE HONG KONG STOCK EXCHANGE
Our A Shares and our H Shares are generally neither interchangeable nor fungible, and the market
prices of our A Shares and our H Shares may be different after the Global Offering. The Guidelines on
Application for ‘‘Full Circulation’’ of Domestic Unlisted Shares of H-share Companies《( H股公司境內
未上市股份申請‘‘全流通’’業務指引》) announced by the CSRC are not applicable to companies dual
listed in the PRC and on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. As of the Latest Practicable Date, there were
no relevant rules or guidelines from the CSRC providing that A Shareholders may convert A shares held
by them into H shares for listing and trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

OVERVIEW
We are a leading integrated provider of precision manufacturing solutions, bringing together tools,
materials and intelligent equipment for key process segments of the global printed circuit board (PCB)
fabrication value chain, primarily including drilling, routing/forming and other related precision
manufacturing processes. We are the world’s largest supplier of drill bits as measured by sales volume
during the Track Record Period, according to Frost & Sullivan. We strive to create greater value for our
customers through high-end intelligent precision manufacturing solutions.
We achieved steady revenue growth during the Track Record Period. Our revenue increased by
19.9% from RMB1,295.1 million in 2023 to RMB1,552.6 million in 2024, and further increased by
34.2% to RMB2,084.2 million in 2025 representing a CAGR of 26.9% from 2023 to 2025. Our gross
profit increased from RMB454.1 million in 2023 to RMB538.5 million in 2024, and further increased by
56.5% to RMB843.0 million in 2025 representing a CAGR of 36.3% from 2023 to 2025, reflecting the
sustained expansion of our business scale and improvements in our overall profitability profile.
BASIS OF PRESENTATION
Our historical financial information has been prepared based on IFRSs Accounting Standards
(‘‘IFRS’’), issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (‘‘IASB’’). The Historical Financial
Information has been prepared on the historical cost basis except for certain financial assets which are
stated at fair value.
The preparation of the historical financial information in conformity with IFRS requires the use of
certain critical accounting estimates. It also requires management to exercise its judgment in the process
of applying our accounting policies. The areas involving a higher degree of judgment or complexity, or
areas where assumptions and estimates are significant to the historical financial information are
disclosed in Note 4 to the Accountants’ Report included in Appendix I to this Prospectus.
KEY FACTORS AFFECTING OUR PERFORMANCE
Our results of operations and financial condition have been, and will continue to be, materially
affected by a number of factors, some of which are outside our control, including the following:
General Factors
. macroeconomic conditions and overall economic growth;
. technological developments in the sectors in which we operate;
– 211 –

=== PAGE 222 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
. the competitive landscape in the markets in which we operate;
. conditions in the downstream markets we serve and the resulting fluctuations in customer
demand; and
. changes in laws and regulations, as well as relevant government policies and initiatives.
Specific Factors
Besides the general factors affecting the industry, our business and results of operations are also
affected by specific factors, including the following major factors:
Global demand in the PCB industry, particularly precision cutting tools
We generate revenues primarily from our comprehensive solutions for the PCB industry,
particularly precision cutting tools. Our revenue increased from RMB1,295.1 million in 2023 to
RMB1,552.6 million in 2024, and further to RMB2,084.2 million in 2025, demonstrating sustained
growth alongside industry expansion. Our business is closely tied to the performance and demand cycles
of PCB manufacturers. According to Frost & Sullivan, the global PCB market, measured by sales
revenue, grew from US$76.9 billion in 2021 to US$84.0 billion in 2025, representing a CAGR of 2.3%
during this period, and is expected to continue expanding steadily from 2026 to 2030, supported by
advancements in AI, data centers, innovative communication technologies, autonomous driving and AR/
VR. As downstream manufacturers upgrade their PCB designs to meet the increasing technical
requirements of these applications, demand for our high-end precision cutting tools correspondingly
increases, reinforcing the strong linkage between our business performance and overall market demand.
See ‘‘ — Year-to-Year Comparison of Results of Operations’’.
Furthermore, in response to growing demand from overseas markets, which is in line with the
global shift of the PCB industry to these regions, we are actively expanding and strengthening our
presence internationally, including through our production bases in Thailand and Germany. During the
Track Record Period, our overseas revenue increased significantly from RMB46.9 million in 2023 to
RMB92.2 million in 2024, and further to RMB192.0 million in 2025, representing 3.6%, 5.9% and 9.2%
of our total revenue for each year, respectively. As part of our strategy to expand our overseas
production capacity and serve global customers with faster response and lower logistics costs, we plan
to scale up our production bases overseas. See ‘‘Future Plans and Use of Proceeds.’’ Consequently,
demand fluctuations in the overseas markets could also impact our business, financial condition and
operational results.
Our ability to effectively manage the supply of raw materials and optimize cost structure
Effective cost management is fundamental to our ability to deliver competitively priced products.
The largest component of our cost of sales is raw materials consumed, which consist mainly of tungsten
carbide, stainless steel wire, film substrates, brush plates and ceramic strips, accounting for 62.3%,
63.8% and 67.2% of our cost of sales in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. The supply and pricing of
these raw materials are influenced by a variety of external factors beyond our control, including supplier
reliability, responsiveness, production scale, and logistics efficiency. To mitigate the impact of price
volatility and supply instability, we have established stringent management mechanisms for the selection
and retention of suppliers. We communicate with suppliers regarding quality standards, and thoroughly
inspect the products received to ensure that they meet all the technical requirements set forth in our
product designs. We may conduct regular or ad hoc on-site inspections of suppliers and require suppliers
to remedy quality issues upon notice. For more details, refer to ‘‘Business — Supply Chain Management
— Our Suppliers — Supplier Selection and Management.’’
With continued business expansion, improving operational efficiency and streamlining production
processes are essential to managing production and operational costs. We aim to leverage economies of
scale through the optimization of our comprehensive portfolio of ‘‘Tools, Materials, and Equipment’’ to
– 212 –

=== PAGE 223 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
lower unit production costs, while actively optimizing workflows and adopting advanced technologies to
enhance productivity. We also invest in employee training and development to enhance skill levels and
operational effectiveness, thereby improving labor utilization and cost efficiency. During the Track
Record Period, our employee benefit expenses included in cost of sales were RMB203.1 million,
RMB230.5 million and RMB311.0 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively, representing about
24.2%, 22.7% and 25.1% of cost of sales in each of those years.
Investment in research and development
Our performance is fundamentally driven by our ability to sustain technological innovation through
continuous research and development. Precision manufacturing technical specifications evolve rapidly in
response to changing customer needs and advances in automation, materials, and digital manufacturing.
To maintain our competitive edge, we consistently invest significant resources in R&D to enhance our
design capabilities, refine production processes, and expand our technology portfolio.
As of December 31, 2025, our R&D team comprised over 400 employees with diverse expertise
across mechanical engineering, control systems, software development and material science. In 2023,
2024 and 2025, our R&D expenses were RMB97.7 million, RMB109.6 million and RMB135.9 million,
respectively. These sustained investments underscore our commitment to advancing precision
manufacturing technologies and developing differentiated solutions that improve performance,
reliability, and cost efficiency of our products.
We believe that a continuous focus in R&D enables us to rapidly translate emerging technologies
into commercially viable solutions, strengthen our intellectual property portfolio, and continuously
enhance our product lineup. Over time, our R&D capabilities will continue to underpin our long-term
growth, driving product innovation, customer satisfaction, and market leadership in precision
manufacturing.
Our ability to enhance customer relationship
Our financial performance is closely tied to our ability to strengthen and deepen relationships with
customers. Strong and enduring customer relationships translate into recurring orders, larger
procurement volumes, and improved revenue visibility. During the Track Record Period, we reinforced
customer engagement through sustained collaboration on their R&D needs and consistent delivery of
high-quality products and services. Successful technical verifications with customers and their supply
chains have strengthened mutual trust and facilitated the transition from prototype validation to mass
production, directly supporting sales growth and stable capacity utilization. By working closely with key
customers through in-depth communication on insights and client needs, we are able to anticipate
technology trends and align our product R&D roadmap with evolving requirements for higher precision,
efficiency, and reliability. This capability not only increases our share of business with existing
customers but also enhances our market recognition and competitiveness in securing long-term supply
programs.
Our comprehensive product portfolio, spanning precision cutting tools, grinding and polishing
materials, functional film materials and intelligent CNC equipment, has also played a pivotal role in
customer expansion. Many customers that initially adopted our cutting tools subsequently expanded
procurement to include other categories within our integrated ‘‘tools-materials-equipment’’ offering. This
one-stop solution creates cross-selling opportunities, which in turn drive our sales volume, support
greater revenue stability and enhance customer stickiness.
During the Track Record Period, these initiatives collectively contributed to both revenue
expansion and margin stability through higher customer retention, growing order sizes and reduced
customer acquisition costs. Our ability to maintain and strengthen these relationships will continue to be
a critical driver of our operational scale and financial performance.

MATERIAL ACCOUNTING POLICY INFORMATION
Some of our accounting policies require us to apply estimates and assumptions as well as complex
judgments relating to accounting items. The estimates and assumptions we use and the judgments we
make in applying our accounting policies have a significant impact on our financial position and results
of operations. Our management continually evaluates such estimates, assumptions and judgments based
on historical experiences and other factors, including expectation of future events that are believed to be
reasonable under the circumstances. During the Track Record Period, there were no material deviations
between management’s key estimates or assumptions and actual results, and we did not make any
material changes to these estimates or assumptions. We do not expect any material changes in these
estimates and assumptions in the foreseeable future.
Set forth below are summaries of the accounting policies that we believe are of critical importance
to us or involve the most significant estimates, assumptions and judgments used in the preparation of
our financial statements. Other significant accounting policies, estimates, assumptions and judgments,
which are important for understanding our financial condition and results of operations, are set forth in
detail in Notes 3 and Note 4 to the Accountants’ Report in Appendix I to this Prospectus.
Revenue recognition
Revenue mainly arises from sales of precision cutting tools, grinding and polishing materials and
functional film materials, intelligent CNC equipment and others:
To determine whether to recognize revenue, we follow a 5-step process:
1. Identifying the contract with a customer
2. Identifying the performance obligations
3. Determining the transaction price
4. Allocating the transaction price to the performance obligations
5. Recognizing revenue when or as performance obligations are satisfied
In all cases, the total transaction price for a contract is allocated amongst the various performance
obligations based on their relative stand-alone selling prices. The transaction price for a contract
excludes any amounts collected on behalf of third parties.
Revenue is recognized either at a point in time, when we satisfy performance obligations by
transferring the promised goods or services to our customers.
Revenue from sale of goods
Revenue from sale of goods between the Group and its customers generally only includes a
performance obligation for the transfer of goods, which is recognized when the performance obligation
has been satisfied at a point in time.
For sales of goods except for equipment, such as precision cutting tools, grinding and polishing
materials, functional film materials and others, revenue is recognized when the Group delivers the
goods, and upon the customer’s receipt, acceptance, or utilization with confirmation of no discrepancies,
the primary risks and rewards associated with ownership of the goods are transferred to the customer.
For sales of equipment, revenue is recognized when the Group delivers the goods, following
confirmation of acceptance or upon meeting the acceptance criteria.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
For overseas sales of goods, revenue is recognized after the Group delivers the goods, obtains the
customs declaration, and transports them to the customer’s designated location, the primary risks and
rewards of ownership of the goods are transferred to the customer.

NON-IFRS FINANCIAL MEASURE
To supplement our consolidated financial statements, which are presented in accordance with
IFRS, we also use adjusted net profit (non-IFRS measure) as additional financial measures, which is not
required by, or presented in accordance with IFRS. We believe the non-IFRS measure facilitates
comparisons of operating performance from year to year and company to company by eliminating
potential impacts of certain items. We believe this measure provides useful information to investors and
others in understanding and evaluating our consolidated results of operations in the same manner as they
help our management. However, such non-IFRS financial measure we presented may not be directly
comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. The use of this non-IFRS measure should
not be considered as substitute for analysis of, our results of operations or financial condition as
reported under IFRS.

Income Tax Expense
Our income tax expense amounted to RMB28.8 million, RMB30.5 million and RMB60.1 million in
2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. We are subject to income tax on an entity basis on profits arising in
or derived from tax jurisdictions in which members of our Group are domiciled and operate. See Note
11 of the Accountants’ Report in Appendix I to this Prospectus.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we did not have any
material dispute with any tax authority.
PRC
Our income tax provision in respect of our operations in the PRC was subject to a statutory tax
rate of 25% on our assessable profits during the Track Record Period, based on the existing legislation,
interpretations and practices in respect thereof. Enterprises that qualify as ‘‘High and New Technology
Enterprises’’ are entitled to a preferential rate of 15% for three years. Our Company and certain of our
PRC subsidiaries are qualified as High and New Technology Enterprises under the relevant PRC laws
and were entitled to preferential EIT rate of 15%. The qualification as a HNTE is subject to review by
the relevant tax authority in the PRC every three years, and we are currently in the process of applying
for the HNTE qualification review for some of our subsidiaries. See Note 11 of the Accountants’ Report
in Appendix I to this Prospectus.
Hong Kong
Our subsidiary domiciled in Hong Kong is subject to a two-tiered income tax rate for taxable
income earned in Hong Kong effectively since 1 April 2018. The first 2 million Hong Kong dollars of
profits earned by the qualifying group entity are subject to be taxed at an income tax rate of 8.25%,
while the remaining profits will be taxed at 16.5%.
Other jurisdictions
Taxation for other overseas subsidiaries is charged at the appropriate current rates of taxation
ruling in the relevant countries.

YEAR-TO-YEAR COMPARISON OF RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Year Ended December 31, 2024 Compared with Year Ended December 31, 2025
Revenue
Our revenue increased by 34.2% from RMB1,552.6 million in 2024 to RMB2,084.2 million in
2025, primarily due to the increase in revenue generated from precision cutting tools.
. Our revenue from precision cutting tools increased by 46.1% from RMB1,191.0 million in
2024 to RMB1,739.9 million in 2025, primarily due to (i) an increase in sales volume from
911.7 million units in 2024 to 1,263.2 million units in 2025, driven by rising demand from
downstream markets such as AI infrastructure, high-performance computing and automotive
electronics, as well as an increase in revenue generated from overseas markets, and (ii) an
increase in ASP from RMB1.31 per unit in 2024 to RMB1.38 per unit in 2025, primarily
attributable to technological upgrades at our downstream customers, which enabled our
continued product mix optimization towards higher-value precision cutting tools and greater
penetration into higher-end market segments.
. Our revenue from grinding and polishing materials increased by 27.7% from RMB150.8
million in 2024 to RMB192.5 million in 2025, primarily due to an increase in sales volume
from 225 thousand units in 2024 to 288 thousand units in 2025, driven by rising demand
from downstream markets such as AI infrastructure, high-performance computing and
automotive electronics, in particular, increased demand for ceramic brushes in 2025.
. Our revenue from functional film materials decreased by 52.5% from RMB155.2 million in
2024 to RMB73.7 million in 2025, primarily due to a decrease in sales volume from 9.1
million units in 2024 to 6.6 million units in 2025 and a decrease in ASP from RMB17.04 per
unit in 2024 to RMB11.20 per unit in 2025, mainly attributable to fluctuations and shortages
in upstream raw material supply for consumer privacy film materials, such as grating-
structured base films, which reduced the production and sales of such products and their
revenue contribution in 2025. The decrease was partially offset by increased sales of our
automotive light control films, driven by our successful development of automotive light
control films with enhanced product performance, including precise light control and reduced
reflective interference.
. Our revenue from intelligent CNC equipment increased by 39.9% from RMB54.9 million in
2024 to RMB76.8 million in 2025, mainly due to (i) an increase in sales volume of our
competitive high-performance products that meet customers’ evolving demands and (ii) our
successful expansion into overseas markets.
Cost of Sales
Our cost of sales increased by 22.4% from RMB1,014.2 million in 2024 to RMB1,241.1 million in
2025, primarily due to an increase in the materials consumed, which was generally in line with our
growth in sales volume.
Gross Profit and Gross Profit Margin
As a result of the foregoing, our gross profit increased by 56.5% from RMB538.5 million in 2024
to RMB843.0 million in 2025. Our gross profit margin increased from 34.7% in 2024 to 40.4% in 2025,
primarily due to an increase in the gross profit margin of our precision cutting tools.

. The gross profit margin from our precision cutting tools increased from 35.0% in 2024 to
41.7% in 2025, primarily due to (i) continued product mix optimization towards higher-
margin precision cutting tools, including coated drill bits and drill bits with a diameter of 0.2
mm or below, both of which are used in higher-end PCB application scenarios, and (ii)
economies of scale and improved production efficiency attributable to increased sales
volume. In particular, among our drill bits, the ASPs of drill bits with a diameter of 0.2 mm
or below and coated drill bits were RMB1.33 per unit and RMB1.35 per unit in 2025,
respectively, representing premiums of approximately 9.0% and 10.7%, respectively, over the
overall ASP of our drill bits of RMB1.22 per unit. Their respective revenue contributions to
our overall drill bits increased from 23.2% and 35.3% in 2024 to 32.4% and 43.7% in 2025,
which improved our pricing level and margin profile and supported the increase in gross
profit margin of our precision cutting tools in 2025.
. The gross profit margin from our grinding and polishing materials remained relatively stable

prices of our grinding and polishing materials from RMB670.28 per unit in 2024 to
RMB668.25 per unit in 2025, as we adopted more competitive pricing in response to market
competition and (ii) an increase in production cost.
. The gross profit margin from our functional film materials decreased from 16.6% in 2024 to

privacy film materials as a result of fluctuations and shortages in upstream raw material
supply, which increased their per-unit cost of sales and (iii) higher per-unit cost of sales of
automotive light control films, which were still at an early stage of production ramp-up in
2025 and had not yet achieved economies of scale.
. The gross profit margin from our intelligent CNC equipment increased from 33.2% in 2024
to 37.6% in 2025, primarily due to an increase in sales of our higher-margin, competitive
high-performance products that meet customers’ evolving demands, as a result of further
product upgrades, enhanced delivery capability and stronger market recognition of our core
equipment products.

We adopt a demand-driven inventory management approach and maintain our inventory levels by
taking into account various factors, including sales forecasts, production cycles, procurement cycles,
purchase prices determined based on procurement scale and expected trends in purchase prices, current
inventory levels and the condition of our production equipment. We also closely monitor our inventory
levels to maintain a healthy inventory ageing profile. During the Track Record Period, a majority of our
inventories were aged within one year, accounting for 88.0%, 89.9% and 93.5% of our total inventories
as of December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively.
Our inventories are stated at the lower of cost and net realizable value at the end of each reporting
period. Net realizable value represents the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business, less
the estimated costs of completion and the estimated costs necessary to make the sale, including selling
expenses and taxes. In determining the provision for inventories, we take into account, among others,
the ageing profile, physical condition, expected utilization or sale of inventories, estimated selling
prices, estimated costs to completion, selling expenses and taxes. We also review the condition of our
inventories at the end of each reporting period and assess whether any inventories are obsolete, defective
or slow-moving. For inventories identified as obsolete, defective or slow-moving, we estimate the net
realizable value based on their expected utilization or sale and prevailing market conditions. For
inventories under normal conditions, we estimate the net realizable value by product type and make
provision for the excess of cost over the net realizable value, if any.

We do not anticipate any material recoverability issues with our trade and notes receivables
primarily because (i) a substantial majority of our trade receivables were aged within one year during
the Track Record Period, and as of December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, our trade receivables aged over
one year amounted to RMB13.3 million, RMB50.3 million and RMB35.5 million, respectively,
representing 2.3%, 7.2% and 3.8% of our trade receivables balances as of the respective dates; (ii) our
trade and notes receivables are mainly due from customers with good credit standing and stable business
relationships with us, and we did not experience any material bad debt loss or large-scale or systematic
credit default by our customers during the Track Record Period; (iii) we assess our customers’ credit
quality before transactions with new customers, including by reviewing their business registration
information, operating status, litigation records and whether they have been listed as dishonest judgment
debtors, and conduct periodic credit rating updates for existing customers; and (iv) we regularly
communicate with customers and monitor payment status, maintain detailed ledgers by customer and
ageing profile, and follow up on overdue receivables through measures such as telephone reminders,
written demand letters and, where necessary, legal actions.
We measure the loss allowance for trade receivables at an amount equal to lifetime expected credit
losses at the end of each reporting period. For receivables with significant balances or receivables for
which there is objective evidence of credit impairment, such as customer bankruptcy, litigation or
serious default, we conduct individual impairment assessment when the expected credit loss provision
based on portfolio assessment does not reflect their actual credit risk. We recognize expected credit
losses and make impairment provision based on the difference between the carrying amount of the
relevant receivables and the present value of their estimated future cash flows.
Based on the foregoing, our Directors are of the view that there was no material recoverability
issue for our trade and notes receivables and that sufficient provision had been made at the end of each
reporting period during the Track Record Period.

Financial assets at fair value through profit or loss
Our financial assets at FVTPL mainly representing investment in structured deposits and wealth
management products (‘‘WMPs’’). Our financial assets at FVTPL increased by 11.7% from RMB541.7
million as of December 31, 2023 to RMB604.9 million as of December 31, 2024, primarily due to an
increase in structured deposits we purchased. Our financial assets at FVTPL decreased by 34.1% from
RMB604.9 million as of December 31, 2024 to RMB398.6 million as of December 31, 2025, primarily
due to a decrease in structured deposits we purchased.
We have adopted a comprehensive set of internal policies and guidelines to manage our
investments in financial assets at FVTPL and FVTOCI. The fund management department formulates
annual investment plans and quotas for the cash management of our surplus funds, including idle
proceeds, after considering our overall funding position and financing environment. The annual
investment quota is reviewed and approved by the Board. Such investments are primarily made in low-
risk, principal-preserving and highly liquid products. Each of our investments in financial assets at
FVOCI and financial assets at FVPL is reported to and approved by our chief financial officer.
Throughout the investment process, the performance of these investments shall be reported to our chief
financial officer and other key management personnel on a monthly basis. Our management team
responsible for such investments has extensive experience in managing the financial aspects of an
enterprise’s operations.
Upon Listing, we intend to continue our investments strictly in accordance with our internal
policies and procedures, Articles of Association and compliance requirements under Chapter 14 of the
Listing Rules.
Our investment strategy related to such products focuses on safeguarding capital, improving fund
utilization efficiency and generating reasonable returns by investing idle funds in bank deposits and
wealth management products issued by financial institutions.
Financial assets at fair value through other comprehensive income
Our financial assets at FVTOCI primarily consisted of (i) transferable large domination certificates

FINANCIAL RISKS DISCLOSURE
We are exposed to a variety of financial risks, including foreign currency risk, price risk, interest
rate risk, credit risk and liquidity risk. Our overall risk management program focuses on the
unpredictability of financial markets and seeks to minimize potential adverse effects on our financial
performance. See Note 40 to the Accountants’ Report in Appendix I to this Prospectus.
Foreign currency risk
Foreign currency risk refers to the risk that the fair value or future cash flows of a financial
instrument will fluctuate because of changes in foreign exchange rates.
Price risk
We are exposed to price risk in respect of financial assets at FVTPL, which mainly include
investments in bank WMPs and structured deposits. We are not exposed to commodity price risk. See
Note 39 to the Accountants’ Report in Appendix I to this Prospectus.
Interest rate risk
Our interest rate risk primarily arises from long-term interest-bearing borrowings, and lease
liabilities. Long-term borrowings issued at variable rates expose us to cash flow interest rate risk. Long-
term borrowings issued at fixed rates, and lease liabilities bearing fixed rates expose us to fair value
interest rate risk.
We have been monitoring the level of interest rates. The increase in the interest rates will increase
the interest costs of borrowings at variable rates, which will further impact our performance.
Credit risk
Credit risk refers to the risk that the counterparty to a financial instrument would fail to discharge
its obligation under the terms of the financial instrument and cause a financial loss to us. Our exposure
to credit risk mainly arises from granting credit to customers in the ordinary course of its operations and
from its investing activities.
Our maximum exposure to credit risk is represented by the carrying amount of each financial asset
measured at amortized cost and trade and notes receivables measured at FVTOCI as disclosed in Note
39 to the Accountants’ Report in Appendix I to this Prospectus. We do not hold any collateral or other
credit enhancements to cover our credit risks associated with our financial assets.
As of 31 December 2023 and 2024 and 2025, we have no credit risk other than financial assets
whose carrying amounts best represent the maximum exposure to credit risk.
Liquidity risk
We aim to maintain sufficient cash and cash equivalents. Due to the dynamic nature of the
underlying businesses, we maintain flexibility in funding by maintaining adequate balances of such.

As of December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, we declared dividends of RMB90.2 million, RMB82.0

FUTURE PLANS AND USE OF PROCEEDS
FUTURE PLANS
See the section headed ‘‘Business — Growth Strategies’’ for a detailed description of our future

USE OF PROCEEDS
We estimate that we will receive net proceeds from the Global Offering of approximately
HK$4,664.8 million, after deducting underwriting commissions, fees and estimated expenses payable by
us in connection with the Global Offering, and at an Offer Price of HK$380.00 per Share, assuming that
the Offer Size Adjustment Option is not exercised.
We currently intend to use the net proceeds from the Global Offering for the purposes and in the
amounts as set out below:
. Approximately 67.5%, or HK$3,148.7 million, of the net proceeds will be used to expand our
domestic and overseas production capacity and further develop our global business. We
assessed the demand outlook for PCB drill bits by reference not only to the headline growth
of the overall PCB market, but also to the structural shift in demand for higher-performance
drill bits, our specific customer demand profile and our capacity planning requirements in
Chinese Mainland and overseas markets. According to Frost & Sullivan, while the global
PCB market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 5.3% from 2026 to 2030, PCB revenue from
server applications and global AI server shipments are expected to grow at CAGRs of 11.2%
and 20.9%, respectively, during the same period, with global AI server shipments expected to
increase from 3.1 million units in 2026 to 6.5 million units in 2030. Compared with
traditional PCB applications, AI infrastructure-related applications generally require higher-
performance PCBs and, accordingly, create stronger demand for PCB drill bits. As the PCB
industry continues to evolve, particularly for PCB products used in AI infrastructure-related
applications, harder substrate materials increase drill-bit wear and shorten the hole-count life
of drill bits. In addition, higher layer counts and greater board thickness have changed our
downstream customers’ drilling processes. For certain thick-board scenarios, customers may
adopt drill bits of different lengths and staged drilling processes, which can result in a
multiple-fold increase in drill-bit usage for processing a single hole compared with
conventional drilling processes. Higher hole density and an increased number of holes per
PCB also increase drill-bit consumption. As a result, we believe demand growth for our drill
bits is expected to exceed the growth rate of the overall PCB market.
Our capacity expansion plan is also supported by our high utilization levels, recent operating
performance, orders on hand and sales forecasts provided by our downstream customers. In
2025, our drill-bit production lines at Liaoxia Area I, Nanyang and Thailand recorded
utilization rates of 94.2%, 99.7% and 98.1%, respectively, indicating that our existing major
drill-bit production facilities were operating at high utilization levels. As of the Latest
Practicable Date, our orders on hand for drill bits exceeded our available supply capacity.
Based on such orders on hand and customer sales forecasts, we expect customer demand
during the relevant ramp-up period to substantially absorb the planned additional capacity of
Liaoxia Area II shortly after its phased ramp-up, and Liaoxia Area II is expected to operate at
a high utilization level by the end of 2026. Accordingly, we expect to ramp up Liaoxia Area
II and implement the relevant production capacity expansion projects progressively by
reference to customer qualification progress, orders on hand, actual and expected customer
demand, utilization levels, product mix and prevailing market conditions. In particular:
o approximately 53.4%, or HK$2,491.0 million, of the net proceeds will be used for the
expansion of our domestic production capacity, primarily through the development of
the first phase of our new DTECH Intelligent Manufacturing Headquarters Base Project
in Dongguan, Chinese Mainland (the ‘‘DTECH Headquarters Project’’). Specifically,

we plan to expand our manufacturing facilities for high-end precision cutting tools as
well as precision manufacturing equipment, including approximately HK$326.8 million
for land use rights, approximately HK$930.9 million for new plant construction and
approximately HK$1,233.3 million for the procurement and installation of major

DTECH Headquarters Project include: (i) increasing our annual designed production
capacity for drill bits and other high value-added precision cutting tools; (ii) enhancing
product specifications and process capabilities for high-end drill bits, including ultra-
small-diameter drill bits, high length-to-diameter ratio drill bits and advanced coated
drill bits; and (iii) improving operational efficiency, production yield, product
consistency and dimensional accuracy through higher automation, in-process inspection
and automatic equipment compensation.
This expansion will enable us to meet growing downstream customer demand with
timely and stable product supply. We intend to increase our output of drill bits and
other high value-added tool products, thereby strengthening our collaboration with
existing customers across various application scenarios and enhancing our overall
market penetration. As of the Latest Practicable Date, the DTECH Headquarters Project
was at the pre-construction stage, and our Board had approved the project. We expect to
complete the relevant internal approval procedures and enter into the formal investment
agreement in June 2026, commence construction in September 2026, complete
construction in August 2029, complete equipment installation and commissioning in
September 2029 and commence commercial production in December 2029. Upon
completion and commencement of operations, the DTECH Headquarters Project is
expected to principally engage in the production of drill bits and is expected to add a
designed production capacity of approximately 70.0 million drill bits per month,
equivalent to approximately 840.0 million drill bits per year. The net proceeds allocated
to the DTECH Headquarters Project are expected to be used for, among other things,
the purchase and installation of major production, testing, transportation and
warehousing equipment and related supporting facilities. In particular, (i) precision
grinding, drilling and forming equipment, including four-station machines, centerless
grinding machines and pin insertion machines, will be used for blank preparation,
fluting/grinding and precision forming in the manufacture of drill bits, (ii) coating
equipment, including vacuum coating equipment, will be used for surface treatment and
coating processes in the manufacture of drill bits, (iii) inspection and testing equipment,
including online inspection equipment, blade-face inspection equipment and
intermediate inspection equipment, will be used for product quality control,
dimensional inspection and performance testing throughout the manufacturing process,
and (iv) transportation and warehousing equipment, including AGV transportation
vehicles and intelligent warehousing systems, will be used for intra-factory logistics,
materials handling and storage management. The material regulatory approvals and
filings required for the DTECH Headquarters Project include project filing procedures,
environmental impact assessment procedures, construction-related permits and the
relevant permits or filings required for production and operation upon commencement
of manufacturing. As of the Latest Practicable Date, the DTECH Headquarters Project
had obtained the relevant project filing from the competent local authority. Based on

approximately HK$135.4 million (Based on the maximum Offer Price of HK$380.00), and the full

ACTIVITIES BY SYNDICATE MEMBERS
The underwriters of the Hong Kong Public Offering and the International Offering (together, the
‘‘Syndicate Members’’) and their affiliates may each individually undertake a variety of activities (as
further described below) which do not form part of the underwriting or stabilizing process. The
Syndicate Members and their affiliates are diversified financial institutions with relationships in
countries around the world. These entities engage in a wide range of commercial and investment
banking, brokerage, funds management, trading, hedging, investing and other activities for their own
account and for the account of others. In the ordinary course of their various business activities, the
Syndicate Members and their respective affiliates may purchase, sell or hold a broad array of
investments and actively trade securities, derivatives, loans, commodities, currencies, credit default
swaps and other financial instruments for their own account and for the accounts of their customers.
Such investment and trading activities may involve or relate to assets, securities and/or instruments of
our Group and/or persons and entities with relationships with our Group and may also include swaps
and other financial instruments entered into for hedging purposes in connection with our Group’s loans
and other debts. In relation to the H Shares, the activities of the Syndicate Members and their affiliates
could include acting as agent for buyers and sellers of the H Shares, entering into transactions with
those buyers and sellers in a principal capacity, including as a lender to initial purchasers of the H
Shares (which financing may be secured by the H Shares) in the Global Offering, proprietary trading in
the H Shares, and entering into over the counter or listed derivative transactions or listed or unlisted
securities transactions (including issuing securities such as derivative warrants listed on a stock
exchange) which have as their underlying assets, assets including the H Shares. Such transactions may
be carried out as bilateral agreements or trades with selected counterparties. Those activities may require
hedging activity by those entities involving, directly or indirectly, the buying and selling of the H
Shares, which may have a negative impact on the trading price of the H Shares. All such activities could
occur in Hong Kong and elsewhere in the world and may result in the Syndicate Members and their
affiliates holding long and/or short positions in the H Shares, in baskets of securities or indices
including the H Shares, in units of funds that may purchase the H Shares, or in derivatives related to
any of the foregoing. In relation to issues by the Syndicate Members or their affiliates of any listed
securities having the H Shares as their underlying securities, whether on the Stock Exchange or on any
other stock exchange, the rules of the stock exchange may require the issuer of those securities (or one
of its affiliates or agents) to act as a market maker or liquidity provider in the security, and this will also
result in hedging activity in the H Shares in most cases. All such activities may occur both during and
after the end of the stabilizing period described in ‘‘Structure of the Global Offering — Stabilization.’’
Such activities may affect the market price or value of the H Shares, the liquidity or trading volume in
the H Shares and the volatility of the price of the H Shares, and the extent to which this occurs from
day to day cannot be estimated. It should be noted that when engaging in any of these activities, the
Syndicate Members will be subject to certain restrictions, including the following: (a) the Syndicate
Members (other than the Stabilization Manager or its affiliates or any person acting for it) must not, in
connection with the distribution of the Offer Shares, effect any transactions (including issuing or
entering into any option or other derivative transactions relating to the Offer Shares), whether in the
open market or otherwise, with a view to stabilizing or maintaining the market price of any of the Offer
Shares at levels other than those which might otherwise prevail in the open market; and (b) the
Syndicate Members must comply with all applicable laws and regulations, including the market
misconduct provisions of the SFO, including the provisions prohibiting insider dealing, false trading,
price rigging and stock market manipulation. Certain of the Syndicate Members or their respective
affiliates have provided from time to time, and expect to provide in the future, investment banking and
other services to our Group and its affiliates for which such Syndicate Members or their respective
affiliates have received or will receive customary fees and commissions. In addition, the Syndicate
Members or their respective affiliates may provide financing to investors to finance their subscriptions
of Offer Shares in the Global Offering.

Shares initially being offered under the Hong Kong Public Offering, 126,300 Shares (representing
approximately 1.00% of the total number of Offer Shares initially being offered under the Global

Shares will represent approximately 3.4% of the total Shares in issue immediately following the
completion of the Global Offering. References in this prospectus to applications, application monies or
the procedures for applications relate solely to the Hong Kong Public Offering.

STRUCTURE OF THE GLOBAL OFFERING
Allocation
Allocation of Offer Shares to investors under the Hong Kong Public Offering will be based solely
on the level of valid applications received under the Hong Kong Public Offering. The basis of allocation
may vary, depending on the number of Hong Kong Offer Shares validly applied for by applicants. Such
allocation could, where appropriate, consist of balloting, which could mean that some applicants may
receive a higher allocation than others who have applied for the same number of Hong Kong Offer
Shares, and those applicants who are not successful in the ballot may not receive any Hong Kong Offer
Shares. For allocation purposes only, the total number of Hong Kong Offer Shares available under the
Hong Kong Public Offering (after taking into account any reallocation referred to below) and after
deducting the number of Overseas Employee Reserved Shares validly applied for under the Overseas
Employee Preferential Offering will be divided equally (to the nearest board lot) into two pools (with
any odd lots being allocated to pool A): pool A and pool B. The Hong Kong Offer Shares in pool A will
be allocated on an equitable basis to valid applicants who have applied for Hong Kong Offer Shares
with an aggregate subscription price of HK$5 million (excluding brokerage, SFC transaction levy,
AFRC transaction levy and the Stock Exchange trading fee payable) or less. The Hong Kong Offer
Shares in pool B will be allocated on an equitable basis to valid applicants who have applied for Hong
Kong Offer Shares with an aggregate subscription price of more than HK$5 million (excluding
brokerage, SFC transaction levy, AFRC transaction levy and the Stock Exchange trading fee payable)
and up to the total value in pool B. Investors should be aware that applications in pool A and
applications in pool B may receive different allocation ratios. If any Hong Kong Offer Shares in one
(but not both) of the pools are unsubscribed, such unsubscribed Hong Kong Offer Shares will be
transferred to the other pool to satisfy demand in that other pool and be allocated accordingly. For the
purpose of the immediately preceding paragraph only, the ‘‘price’’ for Hong Kong Offer Shares means
the price payable on application therefor (without regard to the Offer Price as finally determined).
Applicants can only receive an allocation of Hong Kong Offer Shares from either pool A or pool B and
not from both pools. Multiple or suspected multiple applications under the Hong Kong Public Offering
and any application for more than 568,400 Hong Kong Offer Shares (approximately 50% of the Hong
Kong Offer Shares (excluding the Overseas Employee Reserved Shares) initially available under the
Hong Kong Public Offering excluding the Overseas Employee Reserved Shares) is liable to be rejected.
Reallocation
The Offer Shares to be offered in the Hong Kong Public Offering and the International Offering
may, in certain circumstances, be reallocated as between these offerings at the discretion of the Joint
Sponsor-Overall Coordinators. Subject to the allocation cap described in the subsequent paragraph, the
Joint Sponsor-Overall Coordinators may in their discretion reallocate Offer Shares from the International
Offering to the Hong Kong Public Offering to satisfy valid applications under the Hong Kong Public
Offering. In addition, if the Hong Kong Public Offering is not fully subscribed, the Joint Sponsor-
Overall Coordinators will have the discretion (but shall not be under any obligation) to reallocate to the
International Offering all or any unsubscribed Hong Kong Offer Shares in such amounts as they deem
appropriate. In each case, the additional Offer Shares reallocated to the Hong Kong Public Offering will
be allocated between Pool A and Pool B and the number of Offer Shares allocated to the International
Offering will be correspondingly reduced in such manner as the Joint Sponsor-Overall Coordinators
deem appropriate. In the event of reallocation of Offer Shares between the International Offering and the
Hong Kong Public Offering in the circumstances where (a) the International Offer Shares are fully
subscribed or oversubscribed and the Hong Kong Offer Shares are fully subscribed or oversubscribed
irrespective of the number of times, or (b) the International Offer Shares are undersubscribed and the
Hong Kong Offer Shares are fully subscribed or oversubscribed irrespective of the number of times,
then up to 631,600 Offer Shares may be reallocated from the International Offering to the Hong Kong
Public Offering, so that the total number of Offer Shares available for subscription under the Hong
Kong Public Offering will increase up to 1,894,800 Offer Shares, representing 15.0% of the number of
the Offer Shares initially available under the Global Offering (before any exercise of the Offer Size
Adjustment Option) in accordance with Chapter 4.14 of the Guide. In the circumstance where the

investors generally include brokers, dealers, companies (including fund managers) whose ordinary

effected in accordance with the ‘‘book-building’’ process described in ‘‘— Pricing and Allocation’’
below and based on a number of factors, including the level and timing of demand, the total size of the
relevant investor’s invested assets or equity assets in the relevant sector and whether or not it is
expected that the relevant investor is likely to buy further H Shares and/or hold or sell its H Shares after
the Listing. Such allocation is intended to result in a distribution of the H Shares on a basis which
would lead to the establishment of a solid professional and institutional shareholder base to the benefit
of our Group and the Shareholders as a whole. The Joint Sponsor-Overall Coordinators (for themselves
and on behalf of other Underwriters) may require any investor who has been offered Offer Shares under

provide sufficient information to the Overall Coordinator so as to allow them to identify the relevant
applications under the Hong Kong Public Offering and to ensure that they are excluded from any
allocation of Offer Shares under the International Offering.

THE PRC EMPLOYEE PREFERENTIAL OFFERING
Of the 11,368,800 Offer Shares initially being offered under the International Offering, no more

are being offered out of the International Offer Shares but will not be subject to the clawback
mechanism as set out in ‘‘— Hong Kong Public Offering — Reallocation.’’ As of the Latest Practicable
Date, there were 116 PRC Eligible Employees being eligible to apply for the PRC Employee Reserved
Shares under the PRC Employee Preferential Offering. The PRC Eligible Employees are selected by the
Company by taking into consideration, among others, their seniority, length of employment with the
Group, current position as well as contribution made to the Group. Since all the PRC Eligible
Employees will be PRC residents and could not directly participate in the PRC Employee Preferential
Offering according to relevant applicable PRC laws and regulations, the Company intends to place
certain PRC Employee Reserved Shares to Guotai Junan Financial Products Limited (‘‘GTJA FP’’), to
facilitate the PRC Eligible Employees in participating in the economic exposure to the Global Offering
of the Company through OTC Swaps (as defined below) under the PRC Employee Preferential Offering.
GTJA FP will hold the Offer Shares on a non-discretionary basis for hedging purposes as the single
underlying asset of a delta one back-to-back total return swap transaction (the ‘‘GTJA Back-to-back
TRS1’’) to be entered into between GTJA FP and Guotai Junan Investments (Hong Kong) Limited
(‘‘GTJA INV’’), and GTJA INV shall for hedging purposes enter into a cross-border delta one back-to-
back to-back total return swap transaction (the ‘‘GTJA Back-to-back TRS2’’) with Guotai Haitong
Securities Co., Ltd. (‘‘GTHTS’’), in connection with a total return swap order (the ‘‘GTHT Client
TRS’’) to be entered into by GTHTS and the GTHTS onshore clients (the ‘‘GTHT Onshore Clients’’).
Such GTHT Client TRS is to be fully funded by the GTHT Onshore Clients. The full economic
exposure of the Offer Shares will be passed from GTJA FP to GTJA INV under the GTJA Back-to-back
TRS1, from GTJA INV to GTHTS under the GTJA Back-to-back TRS2, and ultimately from GTHTS to
the GTHT Onshore Clients under the GTHT Client TRS. The GTHT Onshore Clients may exercise an
early termination right to early terminate the GTHT Client TRS at any time from the trade date of the
GTHT Client TRS, which should be on or after the date on which the Offer Shares are listed on the
Stock Exchange. Accordingly, (i) GTHTS may exercise an early termination right to early terminate the
GTJA Back-to-back TRS2 at any time from the trade date of the GTJA Back-to-back TRS2, and (ii)
GTJA INV may exercise an early termination right to early terminate the GTJA Back-to-back TRS1 at
any time from the trade date of the GTJA Back-to-back TRS1, which in each case should be on or after
the date on which the Offer Shares are listed on the Stock Exchange. Upon the final maturity or early
termination of (i) the GTHT Client TRS by the GTHT Onshore Clients, (ii) the GTJA Back-to-back
TRS2 by GTHTS, and (iii) the GTJA Back-to-back TRS1 by GTJA INV, GTJA FP will dispose the
Offer Shares on the secondary market and the GTHT Onshore Clients ultimately will receive a final
termination amount of the GTHT Client TRS, which should have taken into account all the economic
returns or economic loss in relation to the Offer Shares, the fixed amount in relation to the GTJA Back-
to-back TRS1, the GTJA Back-to-back TRS2 and the GTHT Client TRS. GTJA FP will hold the legal
title and the voting right of the Offer Shares by itself and pass through the economic exposure to GTJA
INV, GTHTS and ultimately the GTHT Onshore Clients. Due to its internal policy, GTJA FP will not
exercise the voting right of the Offer Shares during the tenor of the GTJA Back-to-back TRS1 and
GTJA Back-to-back TRS2. The maximum subscription amount of the Offer Shares that any individual
PRC Eligible Employee may indirectly apply for under the PRC Employee Preferential Offering will be
limited to RMB20.0 million (excluding the brokerage, SFC transaction levy, Stock Exchange trading fee
